sample_delivery_exceptions::missing_evid.text: {"gaps":[{"id":"GAP-001","question":"How do delivery exceptions behave in rural areas, and would any of the candidate interventions work there?","impact":"would_refine_scope","why_it_matters":"Every segmented figure available splits only by dwelling type (apartment vs house). Rural deliveries are a distinct operating context — longer drive distances, weaker mobile coverage for SMS, different access issues — and an intervention chosen on apartment-heavy data may not transfer. A stakeholder explicitly raised this and nobody could answer it.","how_to_obtain":"Re-cut the Q2 support ticket summaries and first-attempt success metrics by urban/suburban/rural geography classification, which analytics should be able to derive from delivery postal codes.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-002","question":"How many distinct customers experience repeat exceptions, and what share of total exceptions do they account for?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"The repeat_exception_customers field exists in the metrics table but was never populated — blank, not zero. If exceptions are concentrated in a small set of chronically-mislabelled addresses or buildings, a targeted address/access-data remediation on those accounts is a far cheaper and higher-yield intervention than any platform-wide change. Without this figure the team cannot tell whether the problem is broad or concentrated, which is the single most decision-relevant shape question.","how_to_obtain":"Populate the field: run a customer-level distinct-count and repeat-frequency distribution over Q2 exception events in the warehouse.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-003","question":"What did the pre-arrival notification pilot actually do to first-attempt success?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"The 2024 pilot reported 88.1% vs 87.6% with no randomised control and a post-hoc comparison group; the write-up states the effect cannot be separated from seasonal variation. This is an unmeasured result, not a small one — yet a stakeholder is citing it as proof that 'notifications clearly worked'. Treating it as evidence either way is unsupported.","how_to_obtain":"Run a properly randomised notification holdout in a defined set of routes, with a pre-registered primary metric and a power calculation, accepting the 24-hour warehouse lag in the readout plan.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-004","question":"Does correcting an incomplete or incorrect delivery address actually improve first-attempt success, and by how much?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"The November 2024 spot-check established that 41% of 200 failed deliveries had bad addresses, but corrections were applied by hand with no follow-up measurement — the effect of correction is explicitly unknown. Address error is the largest apartment exception category (37.3%), so address validation is the leading candidate; but its entire case rests on a prevalence figure with no linked outcome. The intervention could plausibly fix the data and not the delivery.","how_to_obtain":"Re-run the spot-check as a small prospective test: correct addresses on a random half of a flagged cohort, hold the other half, and compare next-attempt success after the warehouse lag.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-005","question":"What is the engineering effort and elapsed time to integrate the address validation service into the order path?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"Technical constraints state integration effort has not been estimated and the service has never been called from the order path. Marginal lookup cost is now zero, which removes the FY25 blocker, but an unbounded integration cost still bears on the binding cost-per-delivery constraint and on whether anything can ship this year. Choosing this intervention without a sizing is choosing an unknown.","how_to_obtain":"Ask engineering for a spike and a t-shirt estimate covering order-path integration, and confirm whether the 50 req/s cap is compatible with peak order volume.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-006","question":"What is the current peak and average order rate that would hit the address validation service, and does it fit under 50 requests per second?","impact":"would_refine_scope","why_it_matters":"A hard rate cap is documented but no order-volume figure exists anywhere in the evidence to compare against it. If peak checkout volume exceeds the cap, the design must include queueing or sampling, which changes both the scope and the expected coverage of the intervention.","how_to_obtain":"Pull peak-hour and 95th-percentile order creation rates from the order platform.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-007","question":"What proportion of customers hold a recorded, delivery-category opt-in for automated messaging?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"Governance requires recorded opt-in consent specific to delivery messaging, and explicitly states marketing opt-in does not transfer. No consent-coverage figure appears in any source. If delivery-category consent coverage is low, a notification intervention reaches only a fraction of customers and its ceiling on first-attempt success is correspondingly small — potentially disqualifying it regardless of effect size. The 2024 survey compounds this: all 15 respondents were already marketing opt-ins, so it says nothing about the unconsented majority.","how_to_obtain":"Query the consent platform for the share of active delivery customers with a recorded delivery-notification opt-in, broken out by dwelling type.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-008","question":"What does an exception cost, in support handling time and in redelivery cost per delivery?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"Cost per delivery is named as the binding constraint and any per-delivery cost increase requires finance approval before a pilot. No source states the cost of an exception, the cost of a redelivery attempt, or support handling minutes per ticket. Without these, no intervention can be ranked by return, and none can be shown to finance as cost-neutral or cost-reducing. The cost_per_delivery_index is an index with no absolute anchor.","how_to_obtain":"Finance and support-ops to produce a unit-cost model: average redelivery cost, average support contact handling cost, and the absolute value behind index 100.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-009","question":"What volume of AI-generated customer messages would the exception assistant produce, and what human review capacity would that require?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"Governance requires human review of all AI-generated customer content with no volume exemption. At roughly 5,900 Q2 exception tickets, the review burden is a real staffing cost that nobody has quantified. The VP is pushing to ship this quarter; if review headcount is not costed, the intervention may be operationally impossible under the cost constraint. No source estimates message volume or reviewer throughput.","how_to_obtain":"Model expected message volume from exception counts and pair with a support-ops estimate of seconds-per-review to derive FTE requirement and cost.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-010","question":"What is the independent evidence base for the vendor's claimed 30% reduction in exception handling time?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"The whitepaper states no sample size, baseline, comparison method, or industry, and no independent evaluation exists. It is the only quantitative support for the AI triage option and it carries no evidential weight in its current form. Absence of methodology here is not a minor caveat; it means the option is currently unevidenced.","how_to_obtain":"Request the vendor's underlying study protocol and reference customers, or commission a bounded internal proof-of-concept with a defined baseline.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-011","question":"Has a data protection assessment been started for any vendor in scope, and what is the resulting earliest launch date?","impact":"would_refine_scope","why_it_matters":"Governance sets vendor assessments at six to eight weeks, but no source indicates whether any assessment is in flight for the AI triage vendor or the address validation vendor under its renegotiated contract. This directly bounds what can ship in FY26 and therefore which intervention is realistically prioritisable.","how_to_obtain":"Ask legal-privacy for the current assessment queue status for each candidate vendor.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-012","question":"What do drivers say about the causes of exceptions and about the current exception workflow?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"No driver-side evidence of any kind is connected. Every qualitative input is post-exception customer survey; every operational record is support tickets. Drivers are the population that actually encounters access issues, ambiguous unit numbers and locked gates, and driver workflow simplification is a live candidate that was deferred, not rejected. Choosing between interventions while holding zero evidence from the group that executes the delivery is a structural blind spot, not a detail.","how_to_obtain":"Run driver interviews or a driver survey via delivery-ops; note that works-council consultation is required before driver location data is used for anything resembling performance evaluation, though opinion research does not trigger that.","was_searched":false},{"id":"GAP-013","question":"Why has first-attempt success declined steadily from 91.0% to 87.4% across five quarters, and is the decline concentrated in a segment or category?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"The business objectives document states current first-attempt success is 91% while the analytics series shows 87.4% for the most recent quarter — the objective is anchored to a stale figure. More importantly, no source offers any diagnosis of the sustained deterioration. If the decline is driven by a specific cause (a carrier change, a geography, a category mix shift), the correct intervention is the one that addresses that cause, which may be none of the three on the table.","how_to_obtain":"Analytics to decompose the quarterly trend by segment, exception category and geography, and reconcile the 91% figure in the objectives document with the 87.4% measured value.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-014","question":"How do exception categories break down by time of day, and what share of failures occur outside building or concierge access hours?","impact":"would_refine_scope","why_it_matters":"Ticket data is broken down by category and dwelling type but not by delivery time. Customer feedback points at after-5pm concierge closure as a recurring access cause. If a material share of apartment access failures are simply out-of-hours attempts, a scheduling or routing change addresses them without touching the driver app, address data, or customer messaging — an option not currently on the table.","how_to_obtain":"Cross-tabulate Q2 exception events by attempt timestamp and category in the warehouse.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-015","question":"Does the marketing platform rate limit actually cause delivery SMS to arrive late, and how often?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"Technical constraints state delivery SMS queues behind promotional traffic at peak, and one customer reported a notification arriving after the attempt had already failed. But no measurement of delivery-message latency or late-delivery rate exists. If notifications are frequently arriving too late to be actionable, the notification intervention's realistic effect is far lower than any pilot would suggest, and the fix may be messaging infrastructure rather than more messages.","how_to_obtain":"Instrument send-to-receipt latency on the delivery message stream and report the distribution against actual delivery attempt times.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-016","question":"What is the relationship between exceptions and support contacts — how many exceptions generate a contact, and which categories generate the most?","impact":"would_refine_scope","why_it_matters":"The stated outcome pairs first-attempt success with reduced support escalations, but the two metric series are reported independently and ticket counts are given only by category, never linked to exception volume. An intervention could reduce exceptions in a category that rarely escalates and miss the support goal entirely. The conversion rate from exception to contact per category is not available.","how_to_obtain":"Join exception events to support tickets on order identifier and compute contact rate per exception category and segment.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-017","question":"What are the apartment-versus-house and category-level exception rates in periods before 2026-Q2?","impact":"would_refine_scope","why_it_matters":"Segmented first-attempt success and all ticket category breakdowns exist for a single quarter only. Without a prior period there is no way to tell whether the apartment gap is a worsening problem worth prioritising or a stable structural feature, and no baseline against which a pilot's effect could later be judged.","how_to_obtain":"Backfill the segmented and category-level cuts for at least the prior three quarters from warehouse history.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-018","question":"When exactly does the driver app release lock lift, and what capacity is available after it?","impact":"would_refine_scope","why_it_matters":"Two sources state driver-facing changes cannot ship before Q3 2026, and the FY25 deferral of workflow simplification was tied to a platform migration whose completion status is not reported anywhere. Whether driver-side work is merely delayed or effectively unavailable for FY26 determines whether it belongs in this prioritisation at all.","how_to_obtain":"Confirm with the engineering manager the migration completion date, the lock lift date, and post-lock roadmap capacity.","was_searched":true}]}

sample_delivery_exceptions::recommendati.text: {"recommendation":{"statement":"Prioritise ALT-04: trace and repair the loss of secondary address lines (unit/apartment/suite) between checkout and the delivery label, scoped explicitly to the apartment segment, and pair it with the minimum slice of ALT-03's instrumentation needed to measure it. This is the only candidate that attacks the largest exception category in the worst-performing segment with converging qualitative and ticket evidence, no new vendor, no driver-app dependency, and no per-delivery cost increase. It is a recommendation, not a decision: the effort has not been localised or estimated, so approve a time-boxed localisation spike first and hold the build commitment until the spike reports. If the spike shows the field is lost in a system that cannot be changed before Q3 2026, fall back to ALT-03 rather than to ALT-07.","option_kind":"data_quality","selected_alternative_id":"ALT-04","claims":[{"id":"C1","statement":"Within the apartment segment, address_error is the largest exception category (37.3% of apartment tickets, 921 tickets in 2026-Q2), and the ticket notes attribute it specifically to missing or wrong unit numbers.","claim_type":"fact","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-7ee8d3af","quote":"share_of_segment_percent: 37.3"},{"evidence_id":"EV-7ee8d3af","quote":"note: missing or wrong unit number dominates - synthetic"}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Direct operational ticket record for the most recent measured quarter."},{"id":"C2","statement":"Apartments are the worst-performing dwelling segment: 84.1% first-attempt success against 90.3% for houses in 2026-Q2.","claim_type":"fact","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-d8895eb0","quote":"value: 84.1"},{"evidence_id":"EV-e64aa734","quote":"value: 90.3"}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Two rows of the same metric series, same period, segmented."},{"id":"C3","statement":"Customers independently report entering the unit number at checkout and it not appearing on the package, which points to an internal data defect rather than customer input error.","claim_type":"fact","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-efad4673","quote":"My apartment number is never included even though I entered it at checkout."},{"evidence_id":"EV-b26a6ee3","quote":"Third time the unit number was missing from the package."},{"evidence_id":"EV-6750be5d","quote":"The address label only shows the street number."}],"support_level":"moderate","rationale":"Multiple independent post-exception comments converge with the ticket-category note, but this is self-reported qualitative data; no system trace has confirmed where the field is dropped."},{"id":"C4","statement":"Bad addresses are a documented cause of failed deliveries at scale: a manual review of 200 failed deliveries found 41% had an incomplete or incorrect address.","claim_type":"fact","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-47eef27a","quote":"A manual review of 200 failed deliveries in one metro area found that 41% had an incomplete or incorrect delivery address."}],"support_level":"moderate","rationale":"Single non-randomised spot-check in one metro area; establishes prevalence of the cause, not the size of any fix."},{"id":"C5","statement":"The size of the improvement from correcting addresses has never been measured, so the expected effect of ALT-04 on first-attempt success is unknown.","claim_type":"fact","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-47eef27a","quote":"No follow-up measurement was taken, so the effect of correction on first-attempt success is unknown."}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Stated explicitly in the experiment record; this is the central gap in the recommendation."},{"id":"C6","statement":"Doing nothing (ALT-01) has an observed, worsening cost: first-attempt success fell from 91.0% in 2025-Q2 to 87.4% in 2026-Q2 while delivery-related support contacts rose from 27.4 to 38.2 per 1,000 deliveries.","claim_type":"fact","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-62f8f8ab","quote":"value: 91.0"},{"evidence_id":"EV-7713e46f","quote":"value: 87.4"},{"evidence_id":"EV-fba2af1f","quote":"value: 27.4"},{"evidence_id":"EV-ef605f46","quote":"value: 38.2"}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Four quarters of the same directly observed metric series; the counterfactual is measured, not inferred."},{"id":"C7","statement":"Cost per delivery is the binding constraint and any per-delivery cost increase needs finance approval before a pilot, which disfavours ALT-08 (agent call-outs) and ALT-10 (mandatory human review of every AI message).","claim_type":"business_constraint","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-92455949","quote":"Cost per delivery is the binding constraint this year. Any proposal that increases per-delivery cost requires finance approval before a pilot may begin."}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Stated policy in the current objectives document."},{"id":"C8","statement":"No driver-facing change can ship before Q3 2026, which blocks ALT-02 outright and undermines ALT-05: access notes captured at checkout have no driver-side consumer this cycle.","claim_type":"technical_constraint","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-15beacab","quote":"The driver application release train is locked until Q3 2026. No change to driver-facing screens can ship before the lock lifts."},{"evidence_id":"EV-986b01eb","quote":"\"Whatever we choose, it cannot touch the driver app before Q3. That is not negotiable.\""}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Engineering constraint document plus corroborating engineering-manager statement."},{"id":"C9","statement":"Exception events reach the warehouse up to 24 hours late, so same-day measurement of any pilot is not currently possible; measurement work is a prerequisite for a credible readout on ALT-04.","claim_type":"technical_constraint","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-15beacab","quote":"Delivery exception events land in the warehouse with a lag of up to 24 hours. Same-day measurement of any intervention is not currently possible."}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Explicit platform constraint; applies regardless of which intervention is chosen."},{"id":"C10","statement":"Address data must stay in its region of origin, and any new vendor processing customer data needs a six-to-eight-week data protection assessment — a gate ALT-06 may trip and ALT-11 is explicitly blocked by.","claim_type":"governance_constraint","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-8dfd4e3c","quote":"Customer address data must remain within its region of origin. Cross-region processing requires a documented transfer assessment approved before launch."},{"evidence_id":"EV-8dfd4e3c","quote":"Any new vendor processing customer data requires a completed data protection assessment. Assessments currently take six to eight weeks."}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Current governance policy, owner legal-privacy."},{"id":"C11","statement":"The 2024 pre-arrival notification pilot did not demonstrate an effect; the stakeholder claim that notifications 'clearly worked' is opinion contradicted by the pilot's own record, so ALT-07 rests on preference rather than evidence.","claim_type":"stakeholder_opinion","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-986b01eb","quote":"\"Notifications clearly worked last time. We saw the numbers move. We should just turn them on everywhere.\""}],"opposing_citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-47eef27a","quote":"The pilot had no randomised control group. The comparison group was selected after the fact from deliveries in the same period. The difference is not statistically meaningful, and the notification effect cannot be separated from seasonal variation."},{"evidence_id":"EV-47eef27a","quote":"The survey was sent to 15 customers, all of whom had already opted into SMS marketing."}],"support_level":"low","rationale":"The only backing for ALT-07 is that two stakeholders want it; the underlying pilot and survey do not support the claim."},{"id":"C12","statement":"Broad delivery notification enablement is additionally blocked by consent rules and by messaging throughput shared with promotional sends.","claim_type":"governance_constraint","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-8dfd4e3c","quote":"Automated delivery messaging requires recorded opt-in consent. Consent is not transferable between message categories: marketing opt-in does not authorise delivery notifications."},{"evidence_id":"EV-15beacab","quote":"Delivery SMS is routed through the marketing messaging platform and shares a rate limit with promotional sends. At peak promotional volume, delivery messages queue behind marketing traffic."}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Policy plus platform constraint; both independent of the effect-size question."},{"id":"C13","statement":"The AI options have no usable evidence base: the vendor's 30% claim is uncontrolled and undocumented, and automated exception triage has never been tested internally.","claim_type":"fact","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-986b01eb","quote":"The whitepaper does not state its sample size, baseline, comparison method, or the industry the figure came from. No independent evaluation was provided."},{"evidence_id":"EV-47eef27a","quote":"No experiment has tested driver-side workflow changes, and none has tested automated exception triage."}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Absence of evidence is documented in both the stakeholder notes and the experiment record."},{"id":"C14","statement":"ALT-06's FY25 cost blocker is gone, but its integration cost and elapsed time are unknown and it would be a new critical-path dependency at checkout, so it cannot be sequenced ahead of ALT-04 on current information.","claim_type":"technical_constraint","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-15beacab","quote":"Integration effort has not been estimated. The service has never been called from the order path."},{"evidence_id":"EV-15beacab","quote":"Lookups are now bundled at no marginal cost per call, subject to a hard cap of 50 requests per second."}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Both the removed blocker and the remaining unknowns are stated in the same constraint document."},{"id":"C15","statement":"Repeat-exception customers were never measured, so no option — including ALT-04 — can be justified or targeted on the basis of concentrated harm to high-value customers.","claim_type":"fact","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-8adfb0a2","quote":"synthetic - not measured; field exists but was never populated"}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"The metric row exists with no value; this is a gap common to every alternative."},{"id":"C16","statement":"Rural exception behaviour is unknown, so the recommendation is not evidenced outside the measured apartment/house split.","claim_type":"fact","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-986b01eb","quote":"The Metro West lead asked whether exceptions behave differently in rural areas. Nobody present had the data."}],"support_level":"moderate","rationale":"Recorded as an open question that nobody could answer; limits scope claims."}],"support_level":"moderate","support_basis":"Support is moderate, and only for the apartment segment. It rests on three converging sources for the cause — address_error is 37.3% of apartment exception tickets with unit-number loss named in the ticket notes (EV-7ee8d3af), apartment first-attempt success is 6.2 points below houses (EV-d8895eb0, EV-e64aa734), and multiple post-exception comments describe entering the unit number at checkout and not seeing it on the label (EV-efad4673, EV-b26a6ee3, EV-6750be5d). It is not strong because two things are unmeasured: the effect of correcting an address on first-attempt success (the 2024 spot-check took no follow-up measurement, EV-47eef27a), and the engineering effort, which cannot be estimated until the defect is localised in the order-to-label chain — no estimate exists anywhere in the evidence set, and no cost of an exception has been costed either. Support is comparative as well as absolute: every other option is either blocked (ALT-02, ALT-11), has no measured effect and rests on stakeholder preference (ALT-07), raises per-delivery cost against the binding constraint (ALT-08, ALT-10), lacks a delivery-side consumer this cycle (ALT-05), or is unestimated on the critical path (ALT-06). This claim is evidenced for apartments; it is not evidenced for houses, where address_error is third at 17.0% (EV-beb4932e), nor for rural areas at all.","what_would_change_it":["A localisation spike finding that the secondary address line is NOT being dropped internally — i.e. label fidelity is already high and the loss is at customer input — would move support to low and redirect toward ALT-05 or ALT-06.","A localisation spike finding the loss sits in the driver app or carrier system rather than in our order-to-label path would make ALT-04 unshippable this cycle (EV-15beacab) and promote ALT-03.","An engineering estimate showing the fix exceeds available cycle capacity would move the recommendation to ALT-03 (diagnostic sprint) as the honest use of the quarter.","A randomised follow-up showing address correction produces little or no first-attempt improvement would move support to low for all address-centric options (ALT-04, ALT-06) and raise the relative standing of access-focused work (ALT-09).","Populating repeat_exception_customers (EV-8adfb0a2) and finding harm concentrated in a non-apartment cohort would change the segment scope and could change the recommendation.","A credible estimate for ALT-06 integration showing it is small and can validate address completeness at checkout under the 50 rps cap would make a combined ALT-04 + ALT-06 sequence the stronger plan.","Rural exception data (EV-986b01eb) showing a different dominant cause would refine scope rather than reverse it."],"conditions":["Approve a time-boxed localisation spike (suggest two weeks) before any build commitment. Deliverable: the exact system boundary where the secondary address line is truncated or unmapped, plus an engineering estimate. No estimate exists today; this is the single largest unknown in the recommendation.","Fund the minimum slice of ALT-03 alongside it: a defined pilot cohort with faster-than-24-hour exception event availability, because same-day measurement is currently impossible (EV-15beacab) and without it the pilot cannot be read within the cycle.","Scope the pilot and the success claim to the apartment segment. Do not assert the effect for houses or rural deliveries.","Keep all address processing in region; no vendor is introduced by ALT-04, so no data protection assessment should be triggered — confirm this with legal-privacy before build, not after.","Do not pair this with ALT-07 as a hedge. Delivery-category consent does not exist yet (EV-8dfd4e3c) and the messaging path queues behind promotional traffic (EV-15beacab); adding it would confound the readout and consume the same cycle.","Correct the objectives document's stale 91% figure before the decision is socialised. The measured 2026-Q2 position is 87.4% (EV-7713e46f), so the gap to the 93% goal is 5.6 points, not 2.","Populate repeat_exception_customers as part of the same data work, since it is flagged as recommendation-changing and is cheap to add to an analytics workstream."],"tradeoffs":[{"id":"T1","description":"Choosing ALT-04 attacks the largest apartment cause but leaves access_issue — the largest category across all deliveries at 31.1% — untouched this cycle.","gains":["Targets 37.3% of apartment exception tickets, the worst-performing segment","No vendor, no consent gate, no driver-app dependency, no per-delivery cost"],"gives_up":["Access-issue exceptions (31.1% overall) remain unaddressed","Property-manager access work (ALT-09) is deferred with no evidence gathered on building-level concentration"],"alternative_ids":["ALT-04","ALT-09","ALT-05"]},{"id":"T2","description":"Recommending a build over ALT-03 trades measurement rigour for a quarter of momentum, while metrics continue to decline.","gains":["A shippable change in-cycle against a metric that has fallen every quarter","Avoids spending the cycle producing no customer-facing improvement"],"gives_up":["The randomised address-correction study stays undone, so the effect size remains unknown even after the fix","Rural and repeat-exception gaps stay open unless explicitly funded as conditions"],"alternative_ids":["ALT-03","ALT-04","ALT-01"]},{"id":"T3","description":"Declining ALT-07 and ALT-10/ALT-11 means declining what two stakeholders and a VP are asking for.","gains":["Avoids spending the cycle on an intervention whose only prior test showed no statistically meaningful effect","Avoids compounding consent, review-capacity and vendor-assessment gates"],"gives_up":["Stakeholder goodwill; the VP's stated wish for an AI assistant this quarter goes unmet","Any option value from early AI experience, which would need a separate, properly scoped trial later"],"alternative_ids":["ALT-07","ALT-10","ALT-11"]},{"id":"T4","description":"Choosing an internal data fix over vendor address validation forgoes coverage of address errors that originate with the customer rather than in our pipeline.","gains":["No new critical-path dependency at checkout and no 50 rps cap failure mode","No possible six-to-eight-week vendor assessment delay"],"gives_up":["Typos, wrong street numbers and malformed addresses the customer actually entered wrongly go uncorrected","Delays learning whether validation is cheap now that marginal lookup cost is zero"],"alternative_ids":["ALT-04","ALT-06"]}],"experiment":{"id":"EXP-ALT04-UNIT-FIELD","hypothesis":"Secondary address lines entered at checkout are being lost before label generation for a material share of apartment orders; repairing that loss raises apartment first-attempt success and reduces address_error tickets, with no increase in cost per delivery and no reduction in checkout conversion.","method":"Stage 1 (audit, no customer impact): for a sample of at least 2,000 recent apartment orders where a secondary address line was present at checkout, join the checkout record to the generated label payload and measure the label fidelity rate — the share where unit/apartment/suite survived to the label. This quantifies the defect and localises it to a specific hop in the order-to-label chain. If fidelity is already above roughly 95%, stop: the defect hypothesis is disconfirmed and the recommendation fails here, at low cost. Stage 2 (fix, staggered rollout): deploy the repair by fulfilment node or region in a randomised or matched-stagger design so that untreated nodes act as concurrent controls, rather than comparing to a historical period — this is the specific weakness that made the 2024 notification pilot unreadable. Restrict the primary analysis to apartment-segment deliveries. Instrument the pilot cohort so exception events are available faster than the standard 24-hour warehouse lag; if that cannot be arranged, extend the read window and say so in the readout rather than reading a partial quarter.","duration":"2 weeks for the audit and localisation spike; then 8 weeks of staggered rollout and measurement, given the 24-hour event lag and quarterly ticket reporting cadence.","metrics":[{"name":"Secondary-address-line label fidelity rate (apartment orders)","role":"success","definition":"Share of apartment orders with a secondary address line captured at checkout where that line is present and complete on the generated delivery label.","target":"Rise to at least 98% post-fix, from whatever the Stage 1 audit baseline proves to be.","rationale":"This is the direct mechanism the option claims to repair, and the only metric that can be read quickly and unambiguously. If the baseline is already high, the whole recommendation is falsified in Stage 1."},{"name":"Apartment first-attempt delivery success","role":"success","definition":"First-attempt success for apartment-segment deliveries in treated nodes versus concurrent untreated nodes.","target":"At least +2.0 percentage points versus concurrent control, against the 84.1% 2026-Q2 apartment baseline.","rationale":"The outcome the FY26 goal is written against; the segment baseline is measured (EV-d8895eb0), and the treated-versus-concurrent comparison avoids the after-the-fact control problem that voided the 2024 pilot."},{"name":"Address_error tickets per 1,000 apartment deliveries","role":"success","definition":"Support tickets categorised address_error, normalised per 1,000 apartment deliveries, treated versus control nodes.","target":"Reduction of at least 20% in treated nodes.","rationale":"Ties the fix to the contact-reduction goal and to the 921-ticket apartment address_error volume in the current quarter."},{"name":"Cost per delivery index","role":"guardrail","definition":"Existing cost_per_delivery_index, treated nodes versus control.","target":"No increase above the 2026-Q2 value of 100.0.","rationale":"Cost per delivery is the stated binding constraint; Separately and in parallel, analyse orders per enrolled session in the existing EXP-2026-04 dataset before its 180-day deletion date, and restate 2025 periods under definition v3 so the FY26 target gap can be read cleanly. Pre-agree rollback triggers with Payments Risk and Finance before release.","duration":"Four weeks of holdout at 90/10 for the primary readout; retain the holdout for six weeks if weekly volumes fall short. Chargeback guardrail monitoring continues for 120 days after the last enrolled order, past the freeze.","metrics":[{"name":"payment_auth_completion_percent (Central and South)","role":"success","definition":"Share of sessions entering the payment authorisation step that complete it, treatment arm versus randomised holdout, gateway-log series.","target":"Treatment exceeds holdout by at least +2.0pp with a 95% interval excluding zero; the pre-existing North result predicts approximately +3.4pp.","rationale":"Direct replication of the measured primary effect on the untreated population, using the same metric as EXP-2026-04."},{"name":"orders per enrolled session","role":"success","definition":"Completed orders divided by sessions enrolled at the payment authorisation step, treatment versus holdout. Registered as primary before launch.","target":"Positive and statistically distinguishable from zero; no more than a token fraction of the step-level lift lost downstream.","rationale":"The experiment report states this was recorded but never analysed, so the order-level benefit is currently inferred rather than measured. This closes the single biggest gap in the case."},{"name":"payment processing cost per order","role":"guardrail","definition":"Total processing fees and authorisation-attempt costs attributable to orders originating in enrolled sessions, divided by those orders, split by arm.","target":"Treatment no higher than holdout within measurement noise; any increase triggers finance approval before continuing the ramp.","rationale":"Named as the binding financial constraint in the FY26 objectives, and currently unmeasured for this treatment because the published cost index is a network aggregate across all surfaces."},{"name":"chargeback rate on enrolled sessions, 120-day window","role":"guardrail","definition":"Chargebacks per order originating in enrolled sessions, counted to the full 120 days permitted by scheme rules, by arm.","target":"Treatment within +0.02pp of holdout, matching the interval already observed at 30 days; breach triggers rollback.","rationale":"The existing null was truncated at 30 days against a 120-day dispute window, and is the specific basis of the Payments Risk objection."},{"name":"refund rate on enrolled sessions","role":"guardrail","definition":"Refunds per order originating in enrolled sessions, by arm.","target":"No increase whose 95% interval excludes zero.","rationale":"Second fraud/quality guardrail already read as null in EXP-2026-04 (control 1.83%, treatment 1.86%); confirms the reading holds on new regions."},{"name":"payment-related support contacts per 1,000 orders","role":"guardrail","definition":"Contacts tagged payment_declined_or_error plus order_not_placed_unclear_why, per 1,000 orders, by arm where attributable.","target":"No increase; a decrease would be welcome but is not the success criterion.","rationale":"The prior reading favouring treatment was unregistered and reported for context only, so it is treated here as a harm check rather than a benefit claim."},{"name":"order_confirmation step completion","role":"guardrail","definition":"Share of sessions reaching order confirmation that complete it, by arm.","target":"No degradation from the 99.6% baseline.","rationale":"Guards against the treatment pushing failures downstream rather than removing them — the mechanism by which a step-level lift could fail to produce orders."}]}}}

checkout_error_rate::challenger::v1.text: {"findings":[{"question":"claims_supported","verdict":"concern","explanation":"Most of the load-bearing claims resolve, but two are weaker than stated. (1) C12 uses the 81,500 sessions lost at payment authorisation in 2026-Q2 as the addressable pool, and the source row itself warns that the quarter already contains treatment exposure — so the figure is not a clean untreated baseline and cannot be used as-is to size the remaining opportunity. The draft never discloses this. (2) C2 describes 'five weeks of ramp' at 93.1-95.0%; the 93.1% week was only a 50% ramp, so the full-rollout series is four weeks, not five. Separately, the gateway series is a before/after with a non-randomised comparison group, which is corroboration rather than 'independent replication' in the causal sense the wording implies.","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-39930965","quote":"synthetic - includes six weeks of EXP-2026-04 treatment exposure"},{"evidence_id":"EV-04a161ba","quote":"rollout_state: ramped_50_percent"},{"evidence_id":"EV-33b7280a","quote":"It is produced independently of experiment instrumentation."}]},{"question":"contradictions_considered","verdict":"concern","explanation":"The freeze-date, definition-break and promotion-artefact conflicts are engaged with properly. The slot-selection conflict is not. C13 concedes slot selection loses more sessions (133,000) and then removes it from consideration on a scope claim that the evidence does not support: the objectives document places slot *capacity* out of scope, not the slot interface, and the split between capacity and interface is explicitly unmeasured. The same team shipped a slot picker redesign in February 2026, which shows the interface is actionable by checkout. The largest loss step in the funnel is therefore dismissed on an unresolved question rather than a settled constraint, and no option in the set tests the slot interface with a holdout.","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-8cc44847","quote":"Fulfilment slot capacity is owned by the fulfilment planning team and is not part of the checkout reliability programme."},{"evidence_id":"EV-3424ee59","quote":"synthetic - largest single loss in the funnel; the split between slot unavailability and interface difficulty is not measured"},{"evidence_id":"EV-f71c3028","quote":"A redesigned slot picker was released to all web customers on 2026-02-09 with no holdout group."}]},{"question":"preference_as_evidence","verdict":"concern","explanation":"The draft is disciplined about the two named objections (Brennig, Kovaleva) and about Reddick's all-surfaces demand. But it adopts leadership's framing sentence — that checkout reliability is 'the largest addressable source of lost orders' — as if it were a finding, and uses it together with the scope paragraph to close off the slot step. That sentence is an assertion in a strategy document written by product-leadership and is contradicted by the funnel data on session losses. Repetition of a leadership framing in an objectives document does not make it a measured fact about where the recoverable losses are.","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-8cc44847","quote":"Checkout reliability is treated as the largest addressable source of lost orders this year."},{"evidence_id":"EV-3424ee59","quote":"sessions_lost: 133000"}]},{"question":"non_ai_considered","verdict":"passes","explanation":"The selected option is itself a non-AI UX change, and the two AI options (OPT-08, OPT-09) are assessed on their own dimensions and set aside for documented reasons — no measured benefit over the plain-language messaging already shipped in the treatment, and, for OPT-09, a missing human-review route and unquantified cost-per-attempt exposure against the binding cost constraint. Non-AI alternatives (OPT-05 timeouts, OPT-11 documentation, OPT-06 buy) are each argued rather than listed.","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-e86d8670","quote":"Where an automated risk decision refuses a customer's order, a documented human-review route must exist."}]},{"question":"no_build_considered","verdict":"concern","explanation":"Hold (OPT-02), defer (OPT-10) and research-first (OPT-04) all exist and are assessed across dimensions, and OPT-04 is partly adopted. But the framing is asymmetric. OPT-02's evidence_confidence line dismisses the waiting case as resting on 'an unrecorded claim about past retry mechanisms', while the draft's own support paragraph gives two measured-evidence reasons to wait that OPT-02 is not credited with: the chargeback null is truncated at 30 days against a 120-day window, and cost per order — the constraint leadership calls binding — is not measured anywhere. The strongest form of 'wait' is not 'trust Payments Risk'; it is 'run the order-level and cost analyses first, which are cheap, unaffected by the freeze, and use data that still exists until roughly December'. That version is never priced against shipping now.","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-f71c3028","quote":"Chargebacks were counted to 30 days after order. Scheme rules permit a dispute up to 120 days after the transaction, so the chargeback reading is partial and the series is still being collected."},{"evidence_id":"EV-e86d8670","quote":"Experiment datasets containing payment identifiers are deleted 180 days after the experiment closes."}]},{"question":"overconfident","verdict":"concern","explanation":"'Moderate' is defensible for the step-level result, but the action attached to it goes further than the caveats allow. The desired outcome has three parts — more orders, no fraud increase, no cost-per-order increase — and the plan can verify none of them before release. The cost condition is likely unsatisfiable rather than merely unmet: the only published cost figure is a network aggregate at surface 'all', so the fallback in the conditions ('record that the constraint is unverified and get an explicit decision to proceed anyway') converts a constraint the draft calls binding into a waiver. Ordering also undercuts the stated reasoning: the order-level analysis is named as the reason support is not strong, is unaffected by the freeze, and could be run before rather than 'in parallel' with a network rollout.","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-540bba8d","quote":"metric: payment_processing_cost_index"},{"evidence_id":"EV-8cc44847","quote":"Payment processing cost per order is the binding financial constraint. Any proposal that raises it requires finance approval before rollout."}]},{"question":"what_could_make_it_wrong","verdict":"concern","explanation":"The draft's list is good but misses the most specific mechanism by which a +3.4pp session-level step gain could fail to become orders. In control, a failed authorisation returns the customer to the cart with the form cleared; the session identifier is issued at cart entry, so a customer who re-enters checkout can be counted as a fresh session and re-randomised. Control would then contribute multiple low-quality sessions per customer attempt while treatment recovers inside one session. Under that mechanism the step-completion-per-session lift overstates the per-customer order lift, and orders per enrolled session could move far less than 3.4pp. A second specific failure mode: inline recovery raises authorisation attempts per order, which is exactly the quantity that would raise processing cost per order — the one constraint declared binding and the one thing nobody has measured. A third: the 81,500 loss pool used to size the prize already includes treatment exposure, so the remaining recoverable volume in Central and South may be smaller than presented.","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-f71c3028","quote":"returns the customer to the cart and clears the payment form"},{"evidence_id":"EV-128daebb","quote":"The identifier is now issued once at cart entry."},{"evidence_id":"EV-39930965","quote":"synthetic - includes six weeks of EXP-2026-04 treatment exposure"}]},{"question":"what_to_test","verdict":"concern","explanation":"The proposed test is the rollout itself, with no holdout named in Central or South — which means the two unmeasured outcome criteria (orders per enrolled session, cost per order) stay unmeasurable after release, exactly as they are now. Cheaper, freeze-independent work should come first: the orders-per-enrolled-session and basket-value analysis on the existing EXP-2026-04 dataset, a de-duplicated per-customer-attempt version of the same analysis to check the session-counting risk above, and an authorisation-attempts-per-order count from gateway logs for North treated versus rest-of-network as a proxy for cost per order that does not depend on finance producing a new index. If a rollout proceeds, it should keep a holdout large enough to read orders and chargebacks, with the 120-day chargeback series and a pre-agreed rollback threshold defined before release rather than after.","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-f71c3028","quote":"Order completion per enrolled session was recorded but was not a registered metric and has not been analysed."},{"evidence_id":"EV-5e159e3a","quote":"A change freeze applies to all checkout services from 2026-09-07 to 2026-10-05 for peak trading."}]}],"reclassify":[{"claim_id":"C13","new_type":"assumption","reason":"Labelled a business_constraint, but the evidence only puts slot *capacity* out of scope and assigns it to fulfilment planning. The operative part of the claim — that slot selection 'is not an alternative this team can act on' — is an inference that requires the unmeasured capacity-versus-interface split to fall one way, and is undercut by the team's own February slot picker release. It should carry the epistemic weight of an assumption, not of a constraint that closes the question."},{"claim_id":"C10","new_type":"assumption","reason":"Labelled a governance_constraint, but no compliance determination is in evidence. It is an inference that the described re-presentation mechanism satisfies the tokenisation rule, drawn by reading the experiment description against the policy text. The scheme sign-off that would actually settle it has not been submitted, so this is an assumption the ten-day review could overturn."},{"claim_id":"C12","new_type":"assumption","reason":"Presented as fact that payment authorisation is 'the largest error-driven loss inside the checkout reliability programme' with 81,500 sessions lost. The number is drawn from a quarter that already contains treatment exposure, and the qualifier 'inside the checkout reliability programme' does the work of excluding the larger slot-selection loss by way of the scope assumption in C13. Both the magnitude and the ranking rest on assumptions rather than on a clean measurement."}],"recommended_support":null,"what_would_change_it":["A de-duplicated, per-customer analysis of EXP-2026-04 showing that a material share of control 'failed' sessions were re-entries by the same customer, which would mean the session-level +3.4pp overstates the per-customer order gain.","Authorisation attempts per order rising in North treated traffic relative to rest-of-network, indicating the mechanism raises processing cost per order and putting the rollout in breach of the constraint the objectives document calls binding.","The unmeasured capacity-versus-interface split at slot selection resolving towards interface difficulty, which would make the 133,000-session slot step an actionable alternative and undermine the scoping inference in C13.","An untreated re-baseline of payment-authorisation losses in Central and South showing the recoverable volume is materially below the 81,500 figure, which is contaminated by six weeks of treatment exposure.","Payment-scheme review returning changes rather than a clean sign-off within ten working days, which removes the pre-freeze window the whole urgency argument rests on."],"what_to_test":["Orders per enrolled session and basket value on the existing EXP-2026-04 dataset, run before any rollout decision rather than in parallel with it — it is analytical work, unaffected by the freeze, and the deletion date is months away.","The same order-level analysis repeated at customer-attempt level rather than session level, to test whether control sessions were inflated by cart re-entry under the cart-entry session identifier.","Authorisation attempts per order and gateway fee events for North treated sessions versus rest-of-network, as a cost-per-order proxy that does not depend on finance producing a treated-versus-untreated index that no published record currently supports.","A staged Central/South release with a retained holdout sized to read orders, chargebacks and refunds, with the 120-day chargeback series and rollback threshold agreed before release.","An untreated baseline for payment-authorisation losses in Central and South, to size the remaining opportunity independently of the treatment-contaminated 2026-Q2 funnel row."]}

identity_verification::challenger::v1.text: {"findings":[{"question":"claims_supported","verdict":"concern","explanation":"The core randomised result (C1, C2) and the funnel counts (C3, C4) are quoted accurately. Three claims overstate or misstate their evidence. (a) C5 says abandonment 'has risen monotonically from 38.2% in 2025-07 to 44.2% in 2026-06'. The series is not monotonic: it falls from 38.2 (2025-07) to 37.6 (2025-08) and from 41.7 (2025-12) to 40.8 (2026-01). The net rise is real; 'monotonically' is not, and the same wording is reused in the contradictions section to declare a stakeholder 'contradicted'. That stakeholder said 'ever since we started tracking it', and the warehouse series only begins 2025-07, so the refutation is narrower than stated. The governance policy independently records that platform log access is granted to all 84 engineers and does not meet the named-role requirement, and that an open High finding in the cardholder data environment must be closed before the 2026-10-31 attestation absent an accepted compensating control — of which none has been proposed.","how_to_resolve":"Treat both as opinions, not findings; settle by reference to the register status and the governance rule, and ask risk-and-compliance to state in writing whether the finding can remain open past attestation."},{"id":"C-009","topic":"Whether pen-test remediation should be ranked on the product backlog","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-0e4c2c0a","quote":""Put the pen-test fix on the same backlog as everything else and let the scores decide. The Director of Payments treats each quarter without adaptive retries as an avoidable loss. The governance policy corroborates side A: only one change to a given in-scope component may be in flight, with a ten business day lead time, and a change freeze runs 2026-11-10 to 2027-01-05 from which discretionary product work is not exempt.","how_to_resolve":"Get change-control to confirm the in-flight rule and sequence dates against the 2026-09-15 remediation deadline, the 2026-10-31 attestation, and the freeze window, then state explicitly which quarter adaptive retry work could earliest ship."},{"id":"C-011","topic":"Size of the authorisation uplift available from adaptive retries","kind":"metric_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-0e4c2c0a","quote":"A vendor product circulated by the Director of Payments claims a 2.4 percentage point uplift in authorisation success.","locator":"Vendor briefing"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-7083aa45","quote":"Card retry recovery was 41.6% in the treatment arm against 39.1% in the control arm, over 24,800 eligible failures. The vendor figure carries no baseline, sample size, comparison method or merchant category, and a prior decision paused vendor evaluation partly because no uplift figure had been independently verified.","how_to_resolve":"Require the vendor to state baseline, sample size, comparison method and merchant category, and convert both figures onto a common denominator (authorisation success across all attempts) before comparing; an independent evaluation would settle it."},{"id":"C-012","topic":"Whether the partner authorisation floor is currently being met","kind":"scope_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-0e4c2c0a","quote":"The deck opened with a single number: payment authorisation success, 96.9%, against the 96.0% floor in the partner agreement. metric: failed_authorisation_value_usd
value: 7480557","locator":"payment metrics row 8"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-5219cbf8","quote":"No estimate exists of how much of the failed value is eventually recovered when a buyer whose payment failed returns and completes the order by another route.","locator":"Not covered by this review"},"summary":"A precise $7.48m failed attempted value is reported for 2026-Q2 and is the natural basis for sizing any intervention. payment_retry_reliability::challenger::v.text: {"findings":[{"question":"claims_supported","verdict":"concern","explanation":"The quantitative core is accurate: the 81.8% / $6,121,598 / 71.6% figures, the card count split, the unparsed reason codes, the denominator break and the unpopulated recovery metric all match the cited records. Two load-bearing statements do not. (1) C7 asserts that 'invalid or closed-account failures are not recoverable by re-presentation at all'. The governance policy cited says only that re-presentation is capped at two, must be three business days apart, needs three working days' notice, and that any retry-frequency change needs certification. It says nothing about which failure reasons are recoverable. That is an unevidenced domain inference presented inside a governance_constraint claim. (2) The statement calls OPT-04 'a hard prerequisite for the only option that could actually recover mandate value (OPT-09)'. On the only reason-mix evidence available, invalid-mandate plus closed-account is 33 of 60 records against 19 for insufficient funds, and those 33 are the target of OPT-06 onboarding/re-validation and AUD-2026-006 reference-data work, neither of which requires parsed codes to begin. 'Only option that could recover mandate value' is therefore an overstatement of the prerequisite argument. Separately, C13 cites EV-367e5a44 for the absence of a sizing estimate; the document contains no such statement either way, so the citation evidences nothing (the claim is correctly typed as an assumption, but it is unsupported rather than supported).","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-0089742e","quote":"A failed mandate collection may be re-presented no more than twice."},{"evidence_id":"EV-0089742e","quote":"Any change to collection retry frequency must be certified against the scheme rules before it is enabled."},{"evidence_id":"EV-7083aa45","quote":"22 recorded as mandate no longer valid at the buyer's bank, 19 as insufficient funds, 11 as account closed, and 8 unmapped"},{"evidence_id":"EV-a7cf8004","quote":"share_of_failed_value_percent: 81.8"},{"evidence_id":"EV-367e5a44","quote":"Its reason codes are stored as raw strings and are not parsed, so no failure-reason breakdown exists for mandate collections."}]},{"question":"contradictions_considered","verdict":"passes","explanation":"The recommendation engages the material conflicts rather than dropping them: the count-versus-value framing of 'biggest problem' (C8), the 2026-Q1 denominator break that makes the trend unreadable (C12), the D-2026-02 volume-share rationale being pre-dated by the two worst mandate quarters (C6), the PT-2026-014 'closed from an engineering standpoint' versus register-open dispute (C4, with the retest requirement carried into the conditions), the unverified vendor uplift (C11), and the failed-value figure being an upper bound because post-failure recovery was never instrumented (C10). It also correctly treats the hand-read sample as weak rather than as a breakdown. The stale 97.4% strategy-document figure is not addressed by name, but it is subsumed by the restatement argument and is not decision-relevant here.","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-367e5a44","quote":"from an engineering standpoint the exposure described in PT-2026-014 was closed on 2026-06-12"},{"evidence_id":"EV-9e2b26eb","quote":"\"retested_by_assessor\": false"},{"evidence_id":"EV-c8aafb0e","quote":"not measured - the field exists but was never populated"}]},{"question":"preference_as_evidence","verdict":"passes","explanation":"Senior preference is explicitly quarantined rather than laundered: C11 names the Director of Payments' adaptive-retry preference and the vendor material as 'not evidential support', and the vendor claim's missing baseline, sample size, comparison method and merchant category are recorded. The reciprocal gap is worth noting only for completeness: OPT-12 (model-assisted classification of the same raw return strings) is a direct accelerator for the chosen work and the statement never says why deterministic parsing is preferred to it, but that omission does not weaken the non-AI case.","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-367e5a44","quote":"Mandate collections are assembled in a nightly batch and submitted to the scheme directly."}]},{"question":"no_build_considered","verdict":"concern","explanation":"OPT-01, OPT-02 and OPT-03 exist and are assessed, and OPT-02/OPT-05 are folded into the conditions, so deferral is genuinely engaged. But the research option is not compared on its merits — it appears only as a fallback 'if sizing comes back large'. That inverts the argument: OPT-03 is the option that closes both of the gaps the support statement itself names as holding confidence down (the unscaled 60-record sample and the never-populated recovery metric), and it also sizes how many trade buyers are affected, which OPT-04 does not. OPT-04 parses codes but produces no recovery baseline, so after OPT-04 lands the $6.12m prize is still an upper bound of unknown tightness. Relatedly, the case against OPT-01 rests entirely on OPT-04 consuming no change-control slot; the policy constraint is per-component change control, not analyst and engineer time, and the possibility that remediation evidence-gathering and assessor retest absorb the same scarce capacity is deferred to 'what would change it' rather than argued.","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-c8aafb0e","quote":"not measured - the field exists but was never populated"},{"evidence_id":"EV-0089742e","quote":"only one change to a given in-scope component may be in flight at a time"},{"evidence_id":"EV-42471e2a","quote":"attempted value of authorisations that did not succeed - synthetic"}]},{"question":"overconfident","verdict":"concern","explanation":"Moderate is roughly defensible for a measurement step whose central premise — no mandate failure-reason breakdown exists — is documented outright. Add that effort and cost are wholly unsized and the value-concentration argument runs on share-of-value in a single quarter, and the residual case is 'cheap, low-risk instrumentation of a visibly blind spot' — which supports moderate only because the option is diagnostic rather than a build. But 'will show that the re-presentable subset accounts for a materially larger share than the 19-of-60 hand-read sample implies is negligible' misreads its own evidence — 19 of 60 is roughly a third of failures by count, not negligible — and states no numeric threshold, so it cannot fail. Missing from the test plan entirely: whether return-file records can be joined to mandate references at all for the pre-2025-03 cohort; a person-week estimate for parsing plus historical restatement (the condition asks for one but it is not part of the test); and any sampling of post-failure recovery, without which the parsed value shares still cannot be converted into a recoverable prize.","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-7083aa45","quote":"Reason codes were read by hand from the scheme return file because they are not parsed by any system."},{"evidence_id":"EV-a7cf8004","quote":"average_order_value_usd: 1246.00"},{"evidence_id":"EV-c86c1dbe","quote":"Mandate authorisation records for buyers onboarded before 2025-03 do not record the authorisation channel or the mandate reference returned by the scheme."}]}],"reclassify":[{"claim_id":"C7","new_type":"assumption","reason":"The governance_constraint label is correct only for the re-presentation cap, spacing, notice and certification requirements. The trial record shows waste fell from 3.6% to 2.9% but reports no control stores, a concurrent shelf-life extension by Ashcombe Foods and two store refits, and states the effects cannot be separated. It also notes markdown loss in the trial stores was not reported separately, so the effect on the actual decision metric is unknown.","how_to_resolve":"Re-run the two-stage comparison with randomly assigned control stores, after the April 2026 shelf-life change has bedded in, and report markdown loss as well as waste."},{"id":"C5","topic":"Whether two-stage markdown is affordable within the labour model","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-2a2e9b15","quote":"Two-stage markdown was judged to cost colleague hours the estate does not have.","locator":"D-2025-11"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-e27078c1","quote":"Twelve stores moved from the single 17:00 markdown round to two windows: 25% at 14:00 and 50% at 18:00.","locator":"Two-stage markdown trial (March to May 2026)"},"summary":"The standing decision D-2025-11 (November 2025) rules out two-stage markdown on labour grounds, and the objectives state no proposal may add hours to the store labour model. Engineering states intra-day price changes are impossible on the current EPOS release, and shelf labels exist in only 43 of 412 stores. Governance additionally forbids a till price change taking effect before the shelf edge is updated.","how_to_resolve":"Ask Verdant whether the product can operate against a nightly price file and non-ESL stores; otherwise treat it as blocked until the intra-day EPOS release ships beyond its Q1 2027 pilot."},{"id":"C7","topic":"Halcyon Shelf Intelligence data prerequisites","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-cb840f63","quote":"Halcyon Shelf Intelligence consumes item-level remaining shelf life from your inventory system and returns a recommended reduction schedule to the store handheld.","locator":"Halcyon Retail Labs"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-935708d5","quote":"There is no supplier or inventory feed of item-level remaining shelf life.","locator":"Expiry data"},"summary":"Halcyon's product depends on an item-level remaining shelf life feed. The handheld route is also constrained: each store shares one device.","how_to_resolve":"Scope what it would cost to create an item-level expiry feed or enforce fixture scanning, and confirm with Halcyon whether their input can be partial or scan-derived. Two conditions are material, not cosmetic. First, the case for ALT-04 rests on a cross-format correlation between compliance and loss that is confounded (68 neighbourhood stores divert unsold stock to a redistribution partnership recorded as waste; 31 of the 43 ESL stores are high street; high street spends the most colleague hours per week yet has near-worst compliance), so the effect size is unknown and could be near zero. Second, the labour input has not been measured: no evidence records how many colleague hours any candidate intervention adds or removes, and no unit economics for a point of markdown or a point of waste were ever presented, so the return cannot be sized before the trial reads. I also recommend funding the till marked-down-sale flag from ALT-06 in parallel out of the same envelope — without it there is no markdown-to-sale conversion measure and no intervention in this set can ever be attributed. If the product manager will not accept an unsized effect, ALT-03 (controlled trial only) is the honest fallback; it buys attribution and forgoes any FY26 loss reduction.
