returns_fraud_signals::contradictions::v.text: {"contradictions":[{"id":"C1","topic":"How many consecutive quarters the return rate has risen","kind":"metric_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-0560101f","quote":"It has gone up six quarters running.","locator":"Priya Raman, Chief Merchant"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-a48bba41","quote":"value: 11.2","locator":"period: 2025-Q1, metric: return_rate_percent, segment: all — earliest retained point in the series"},"summary":"The Chief Merchant asserts six consecutive quarterly increases. The retained series contains only six quarterly observations (2025-Q1 11.2 per EV-a48bba41 through 2026-Q2 14.8 per EV-14ebd907), i.e. five observed increases; a sixth consecutive increase would require a 2024-Q4 figure that is not in evidence. The programme document makes the narrower claim that the rate 'has risen in every quarter since the start of FY26' (EV-8f056b74).","how_to_resolve":"Ask analytics whether a 2024-Q4 total return rate exists in any retained source. If it does, publish it and the count is settled; if it does not, restate the claim as five increases across six retained quarters."},{"id":"C2","topic":"Whether $4.2M is a measured loss from returns abuse","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-8f056b74","quote":"Returns abuse costs the business $4.2M a year.","locator":"Why this programme exists"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-6d6576ca","quote":"The estimate is a benchmark transposed onto our refund total.","locator":"What this figure is not"},"summary":"The objectives document and the review call state $4.2M as an established annual loss and a recovery target. The finance memo that produced the number says it is an external benchmark midpoint (range $1.1M–$6.3M) applied to Alderwick's refund total, explicitly 'not a measurement of Alderwick's losses', and notes the midpoint has been requoted without its range.","how_to_resolve":"Either fund the deferred $60,000 inspection audit of a random sample of returned units to produce an internal abuse rate, or restate the planning figure as a range ($1.1M–$6.3M) with its source attached before it is used to size any business case."},{"id":"C3","topic":"Whether return rate can measure returns abuse","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-8f056b74","quote":"Return rate is the programme's headline measure of returns abuse.","locator":"Why this programme exists"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-6d6576ca","quote":"No internal measurement of abusive returns exists.","locator":"What this figure is not"},"summary":"The programme designates total return rate as the metric against which it will be judged, treating movement in it as movement in abuse. Finance states no system distinguishes an abusive return from a legitimate one, and returns operations states there is no field or reason code in which abuse could be recorded (EV-7f0a7541: 'no reason code exists for suspected abuse and an associate has no field in which to record one').","how_to_resolve":"Decide and document whether the programme is judged on total return rate (a volume measure) or on a measured abuse rate. If the latter, a measurement instrument — sample inspection or an abuse reason code plus case record — has to exist before the target is set."},{"id":"C4","topic":"What is driving the rise in total return rate","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-0560101f","quote":"It has gone up six quarters running. That is abuse,","locator":"Priya Raman, Chief Merchant"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-53319f96","quote":"value: 46.0","locator":"period: 2026-Q2, metric: apparel_share_of_units_sold, segment: all"},"summary":"One account attributes the rising total return rate to abuse. The mix data offers an unexcluded alternative: apparel's share of units sold rose from 31.0% in 2025-Q1 (EV-08a56377) to 46.0% in 2026-Q2 (EV-53319f96), and apparel returns at 21.3% versus hardgoods at 6.2% (EV-bba87282, EV-7f97e118), so total return rate can rise on mix alone. Research participants describe the behaviour as size distrust, not policy gaming (EV-5a5c4c77).","how_to_resolve":"Run a mix-adjusted decomposition of the total return rate: hold category shares at 2025-Q1 weights and recompute the series. That separates mix shift from within-category change. Category return rates before 2026-Q2 were not retained (EV-bba87282), so this may require rebuilding history from transaction data."},{"id":"C5","topic":"Which segment the leading return reason describes","kind":"scope_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-cd60110b","quote":"share_of_returns_percent: 34.1","locator":"2026-Q2, segment: all, reason_code: did_not_fit"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-d237cb24","quote":"share_of_returns_percent: 58.0","locator":"2026-Q2, segment: tarnside_line, reason_code: did_not_fit"},"summary":"Both figures are true of different populations. 'Did not fit' is 34.1% of all returns, 42.0% of apparel returns (EV-90cf9883), and 58.0% of Tarnside-line returns (EV-d237cb24). Any statement that fit is 'the leading cause' must name which of the three segments it describes, because the implied size of the opportunity differs by roughly a factor of two.","how_to_resolve":"State the segment alongside every 'leading reason' claim, and size each in absolute returned units rather than share, so the all-returns, apparel and Tarnside views can be compared on the same base."},{"id":"C6","topic":"Whether reason-code data identifies why items come back","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-cd60110b","quote":"reason_code: did_not_fit","locator":"2026-Q2, segment: all — 63,600 returns, 34.1%"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-0560101f","quote":"the system records 'changed mind'","locator":"Dana Okonkwo, Director, Returns Operations"},"summary":"The reason-code table is the only available breakdown of return causes and is being read as such. Returns Operations states the codes are the customer's self-selected words with no verification and no code for suspected abuse, so a return an associate believes is fraudulent is logged under an innocuous code. Each row carries 'capture_method: customer-selected at initiation, not verified'.","how_to_resolve":"Validate the codes against physical inspection on a sample: inspect a random set of returned units and compare the observed condition with the customer-selected code. That yields a misclassification rate and tells you how far the table can be trusted."},{"id":"C7","topic":"Cause of Tarnside returns: wardrobing versus a wrong size chart","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-0560101f","quote":"We took back four Tarnside shells last month that had clearly been worn.","locator":"Marcus Delaney, Store Manager, Fairhaven"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-5a5c4c77","quote":"Fourteen differed by more than one size increment, and all fourteen are in the","locator":"Finding 2 — size-chart audit (Tarnside line, introduced 2025-Q3)"},"summary":"One store manager reads worn Tarnside returns as wardrobing and 'would bet it is most of what we are seeing'; he did not have his store's total return count to hand. The size-chart audit finds fourteen mismeasured SKUs all in the Tarnside line, and Tarnside returns are 58% 'did not fit' (EV-d237cb24). The audit itself states it does not establish how many returns the chart error causes.","how_to_resolve":"Pull Tarnside returned units for one period, inspect a random sample for signs of wear, and join the affected fourteen SKUs to their actual return volumes. That gives a split between worn-return and fit-failure volume on the same line."},{"id":"C8","topic":"Whether the receipt-required trial reduced returns","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-0560101f","quote":"When we required receipts in the four pilot stores last autumn the returns stopped almost","locator":"Aaron Bexley, District Manager, District 4"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-3d2cd42c","quote":"any change in return volumes cannot be separated from the drop in traffic.","locator":"D-2025-08 — Receipt-required returns trial, rolled back"},"summary":"A district manager cites the autumn 2025 receipt trial as evidence that receipt requirements work and should not have been rolled back. The rollback record states no returns data was collected during the trial window, no comparison stores were selected, and the four pilot stores were mid-remodel with reduced footfall, so any observed drop is confounded.","how_to_resolve":"If the intervention is reconsidered, rerun it as a controlled test: pre-registered comparison stores, no concurrent remodel, returns data captured for the window. Nothing in the 2025 trial can be recovered to settle this retrospectively."},{"id":"C9","topic":"Whether the data the vendor requires exists","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-1904f23d","quote":"Orlin requires a nightly feed of 24 months of unified customer purchase and return history,","locator":"Deployment requirements"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-3d2cd42c","quote":"online channels, and no per-customer view of returns exists in any system.","locator":"D-2026-03 — Returns data mart deferred to FY28"},"summary":"The vendor's deployment prerequisite is 24 months of channel-unified customer history keyed to a single identifier. The data mart that would join store and online return history is deferred to FY28, no per-customer view exists today, and online item-level detail from the returns portal exists only from 2026-Q1 (EV-3d2cd42c, D-2026-04) — under six months, not 24. Loss prevention reports the same gap ('If someone buys online and returns in store... I have no way to connect it').","how_to_resolve":"Ask the vendor for measured performance on unlinked, six-month, single-channel data rather than 'degrades gracefully'. Alternatively cost the identity-resolution work needed to satisfy the prerequisite and compare it against the FY28 data mart timeline."},{"id":"C10","topic":"Whether the vendor's precision claim can be validated here","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-1904f23d","quote":"The model identifies high-risk returners with 91% precision.","locator":"Claims made in the deck; scored against 'confirmed cases'"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-2d12e461","quote":"field added to the returns dashboard in 2026-Q2 and never populated","locator":"2026-Q2, metric: confirmed_abuse_cases, segment: all"},"summary":"Precision is quoted against 'confirmed cases'. Alderwick has no confirmed cases: the confirmed_abuse_cases metric has no value and there is no case management system in which an abuse case could be opened. The vendor notes concede this ('Alderwick has no confirmed cases'), and the 23% fraud-reduction claim has no definition, baseline, named client or method.","how_to_resolve":"Require the underlying study with defined outcome, baseline and measurement method, plus a specialty-outdoor reference. Independently, establish a local ground-truth set (inspected sample or a populated abuse case record) before any accuracy claim can be tested on Alderwick data."},{"id":"C11","topic":"Whether customer risk scores can be used at the point of return","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-1904f23d","quote":"an action at the point of return: accept, inspect, or refuse.","locator":"What the product is — per-customer risk score"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-829d33e0","quote":"A return may not be refused, restricted, or fee-charged on the basis of an automated score","locator":"Automated decisions about customers"},"summary":"The product scores the returning customer and recommends accept/inspect/refuse at the counter. Policy prohibits refusal on the basis of an automated score without documented human review and an appeal path, prohibits display of customer-level risk indicators to associates at the point of service, and requires inspection to be triggered by 'a property of the item or the transaction, not by a characterisation of the customer'. A new processor also requires a data protection assessment (six to eight weeks) that has not been started.","how_to_resolve":"Legal and privacy review of the specific deployment: whether an item- or transaction-level trigger with a hidden score and a human-review-plus-appeal wrapper is permissible. Start the data protection assessment now, since its six-to-eight week duration gates any transfer regardless of outcome."},{"id":"C12","topic":"Which period's refund base the $4.2M loss figure belongs to","kind":"temporal_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-6d6576ca","quote":"Estimated annual loss from returns abuse: **$4.2M**.","locator":"Headline — 5.9% applied to the FY26 refund total of $71.2M"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-fe9e631a","quote":"value: 23.6","locator":"period: 2026-Q2, metric: refund_value_usd_millions, segment: all"},"summary":"Both are correct for their period. The $4.2M is 5.9% of the FY26 (calendar 2025) refund total of $71.2M, which matches the 2025 quarterly rows (15.8 + 16.4 + 18.6 + 20.4). FY27 refunds are running higher: $22.1M in 2026-Q1 (EV-f8ae13be) and $23.6M in 2026-Q2, i.e. $45.7M in the first half. Quoted as the FY27 loss without restatement, the $4.2M is stale — it belongs to the FY26 refund base.","how_to_resolve":"Restate the benchmark against a current annualised refund base and carry the 1.5%–8.8% range through, or label the $4.2M explicitly as an FY26-base estimate wherever it appears in FY27 planning."},{"id":"C13","topic":"Whether channel-level returns visibility exists","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-0560101f","quote":"My instinct is that the online channel is far worse than the stores, but I have never been","locator":"Nell Faraday, Regional Loss Prevention"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-47808bde","quote":"value: 21.0","locator":"period: 2026-Q2, metric: return_rate_percent, segment: online"},"summary":"Loss prevention describes the online-versus-store comparison as something it has never been able to look at. Analytics already publishes it for 2026-Q2: online 21.0% against store 9.7% (EV-7f296027). The gap that genuinely does not exist is per-customer linkage across channels (EV-3d2cd42c), not channel-level aggregates — two different claims that are being merged into one.","how_to_resolve":"Share the existing channel-level return rate series with loss prevention and confirm what is actually missing. Then scope the remaining need explicitly as per-customer cross-channel linkage, which is the FY28 data mart dependency."}]}

returns_fraud_signals::missing_evidence:.text: {"gaps":[{"id":"GAP-01","question":"What share of Alderwick's returns is actually abusive, and what does that abuse cost?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"Every intervention in play is sized against the $4.2M figure, which is a trade-body benchmark (5.9% of refund value, range 1.5%-8.8%, i.e. $1.1M-$6.3M) transposed onto Alderwick's refund total. Nothing internal distinguishes an abusive return from a legitimate one. If true losses sit near the bottom of the range, a $180k/yr scoring platform with a 24-month minimum term is not payback-positive at all; if near the top, a heavier intervention is justified. The confirmed_abuse_cases field was added to the dashboard in 2026-Q2 and never populated, and there is no case management system in which a case could be opened — blank here means 'never measured', not 'zero abuse'.","how_to_obtain":"Fund the physical inspection audit of a random sample of returned units that FP&A requested in March 2026 and that was not scheduled ($60,000, one quarter, eight stores plus the returns hub). Add an associate-facing disposition field so suspected abuse can be recorded at the point of processing.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-02","question":"How much of the rise in return rate from 11.2% to 14.8% is explained by the shift in mix toward apparel rather than by any change in customer behaviour?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"Apparel share of units sold rose from 31.0% to 46.0% over the same six quarters that total return rate rose, and apparel returns at 21.3% versus hardgoods at 6.2%. A mix-adjusted or within-category return-rate series would show whether behaviour changed at all. Category-level return rates before 2026-Q2 were not retained, so the series cannot be decomposed. The programme treats return rate as the headline measure of abuse; if the rise is mix, the premise for prioritising an anti-abuse intervention over a merchandising fix collapses.","how_to_obtain":"Reconstruct category-level return rates from transaction records for 2025-Q1 onward if line-item history survives, or compute a mix-standardised return rate. Ask analytics whether the underlying rows still exist even though the aggregated series was not retained.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-03","question":"What is the return rate and abuse exposure of the online channel specifically, over time, and how does the same customer's behaviour span store and online?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"Online return rate is 21.0% against store 9.7% at 45% of units, and Loss Prevention's stated instinct is that online is far worse — but they say they have never been able to look. There is exactly one quarter of channel-split data and no cross-channel customer view: the returns data mart was deferred to FY28, so return history cannot be joined across channels, and Larkspur item-level detail exists only from 2026-Q1. An intervention aimed at store associates and one aimed at the online funnel are different programmes.","how_to_obtain":"Channel-split return rate time series from POS and Larkspur summary files; a scoped one-off identity-resolution exercise on loyalty-linked transactions to estimate what fraction of returners are cross-channel, without waiting for the FY28 data mart.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-04","question":"What would each candidate intervention cost to build and run, and what is the internal effort available to run it with no added loss-prevention headcount?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"Only one option has any priced figure at all — Orlin at $180,000/yr plus $0.11 per scored return, which on 186,500 quarterly returns adds roughly $82k/yr in variable cost and exceeds the $50,000 CFO approval threshold. No cost has been produced for a size-chart remediation, an inspection protocol, an associate disposition field, reason-code redesign, or the manual human-review capacity that governance requires for any score-driven refusal. FY27 adds no headcount, so an option whose running cost is mostly labour may be undeliverable regardless of price.","how_to_obtain":"Ask each candidate owner (data-platform, returns-operations, merchandising, e-commerce) for a build estimate and a steady-state FTE estimate; cost the human-review queue implied by governance from expected refusal volume.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-05","question":"What would a restocking fee, a receipt requirement, or any policy tightening save, and what would it cost in lost legitimate sales and loyalty attrition?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"The restocking fee was rejected in January 2026 explicitly without a cost-benefit review, so no estimate exists of savings or of sales impact. The receipt-required trial was rolled back with no returns data collected, no comparison stores, and a concurrent remodel that reduced footfall — it is an unmeasured result, not a null one, yet a district manager cites it on the call as evidence that returns 'stopped almost overnight'. Without an elasticity estimate, the programme cannot know whether it is trading $1 of prevented abuse for more than $1 of lost sales, which is exactly the 'without degrading the experience for legitimate customers' constraint.","how_to_obtain":"Re-run the receipt or fee trial as a controlled test with matched comparison stores and pre-registered metrics, or commission a conjoint/willingness-to-return study. Note the loyalty terms constrain fees, so test the design legal would actually permit.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-06","question":"How many returns would a size-chart fix on the Tarnside line actually prevent, and what is the sales-weighted exposure?","impact":"would_refine_scope","why_it_matters":"Tarnside shows 58% did_not_fit against 42% for apparel overall, and 14 of 40 audited SKUs deviate by more than one size increment — all Tarnside. But the audit did not weight SKUs by sales volume and made no link between affected SKUs and actual return volumes. Without that link, the size-chart route cannot be sized against the scoring platform, and it is formally out of the programme's remit (Merchandising owns size-chart governance) so an escalation would need a number to justify it.","how_to_obtain":"Join the 14 deviating SKUs to unit sales and returned units for 2026-Q2; extend the measurement audit to a volume-weighted sample of the Tarnside range.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-07","question":"How accurate are customer-selected return reason codes, and what would associates record if given a field?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"All reason-code shares carry the caveat 'customer-selected at initiation, not verified', there is no code for suspected abuse, and Returns Operations states an associate certain of fraud processes the return anyway and the system records 'changed mind'. The 34.1% did_not_fit and 12% changed_mind figures are therefore unusable as a split between merchandising causes and abuse, yet they are the only causal-looking data available.","how_to_obtain":"Compare customer-stated reason against physical inspection disposition on the audit sample in GAP-01; pilot an associate disposition field in a handful of stores and measure how often it diverges from the customer's code.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-08","question":"Is the abuse concentrated in a small number of customers, or spread thinly across many?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"A per-customer scoring platform only pays if losses concentrate in identifiable repeat returners. No per-customer view of returns exists in any system, so the distribution of returns per customer is unknown; the only signal is one store manager's recollection of a customer returning fourteen items in March. If abuse is diffuse, customer-level scoring is the wrong instrument regardless of vendor quality, and item- or transaction-level controls are the better fit — which is also what governance requires for anything shown to associates.","how_to_obtain":"Compute a returns-per-loyalty-ID distribution within the online channel alone, where Larkspur item-level data exists from 2026-Q1, as a partial proxy while the data mart is deferred.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-09","question":"Would Orlin pass a data protection assessment, could the deployment be lawful given regional data-residency rules, and how long would clearance take?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"Legal and privacy have not been engaged and no assessment has been started; assessments take six to eight weeks. Governance prohibits transferring returns and purchase data outside its region of origin or using it to train a model hosted outside that region, and prohibits displaying customer-level risk indicators to associates at the point of service — which is precisely what the product's accept/inspect/refuse recommendation does. There is no evidence on whether Orlin's hosting region or its associate-facing UI can be made compliant. If it cannot, the option is not merely weaker, it is unavailable.","how_to_obtain":"Start the data protection assessment now; ask Orlin in writing for hosting region, training-data handling, and whether the associate-facing output can be reduced to an item- or transaction-triggered inspection prompt with no customer characterisation.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-10","question":"What evidence exists that Orlin's product works in a retailer resembling Alderwick?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"The 23% fraud-reduction claim has no definition, no baseline, no named client and no described measurement; the underlying study was promised but not supplied. The 91% precision figure is scored against 'confirmed cases', which Alderwick does not have and therefore cannot reproduce. No reference customer in specialty outdoor retail was offered, and the two case studies are consumer electronics. The payback-in-five-months claim uses Alderwick's own unverified $4.2M. Absence of any independent performance evidence should cap how firmly this option is backed, whatever else is decided.","how_to_obtain":"Require the underlying study, a named reference in comparable assortment and price point, and a paid short-term pilot with a pre-agreed success metric before any 24-month commitment. Note no pilot pricing was offered, which is itself a term to negotiate.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-11","question":"What is the current returns processing cost per unit, and what is the cost of an inspection?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"An FY27 goal is to hold returns processing cost per unit flat or lower, but no baseline for that metric appears anywhere in the evidence — the field simply does not exist in the metrics set. {"recommendation":{"statement":"Prioritise ALT-3: fund the $60,000 single-quarter physical inspection audit of a random sample of returned units across eight stores and the returns hub, and treat it as the gating deliverable for every other option. Nothing in the pack sizes returns abuse at Alderwick — the only loss figure in circulation is an external benchmark midpoint transposed onto the FY26 refund base — so no restriction, vendor scoring, or rules threshold can currently be sized, targeted, or evaluated. Two riders: (a) attach a minimal capture of audit findings (item condition, reason-code discordance) so the results have a home, since no field or case record exists today — this is the cheap subset of ALT-4, not the full POS/portal build, whose cost is unquantified in the evidence; (b) in parallel, at zero marginal cost, have Analytics decompose the 11.2%→14.8% return-rate rise into category-mix effect versus within-category change, because apparel's share of units sold moved 31.0%→46.0% while apparel returns at 21.3% against hardgoods at 6.2%, and mix alone could explain much of the trend the programme is treating as proven abuse. Recommend explicitly deferring ALT-9 (Orlin) in FY27: it requires 24 months of channel-unified history that does not exist, its precision claim is scored against confirmed cases Alderwick does not have, and it conflicts with governance on automated refusal and point-of-service customer indicators. {"contradictions":[{"id":"C1","topic":"Search-to-cart conversion: 12.4% quoted in prose vs 10.7% in the current metric series","kind":"metric_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-843a50ab","quote":"Search-to-cart conversion of 12.4% against a 13.5% FY26 target. metric: search_to_cart_rate
value: 10.7","locator":"search metrics row 1"},"summary":"The July 2026 review slides and the May roadmap both state current search-to-cart conversion as 12.4%, but the analytics series puts 2026-Q2 at 10.7%, 2026-Q1 at 11.0% and 2025-Q4 at 11.6%. 12.4% is the 2025-Q2 value in the same series, so the prose figure appears stale by four quarters rather than wrong: it belongs to 2025-Q2, not to the period the slides describe.","how_to_resolve":"Ask analytics to confirm which period and definition the 12.4% figure was drawn from, then restate the roadmap and slide 2 against the current 2026-Q2 value. The series row EV-cffaa0f1 (2025-Q2, 12.4%) is the candidate origin."},{"id":"C2","topic":"Prior-period conversion figure quoted as 'today'","kind":"temporal_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-a2654f30","quote":"Search-to-cart conversion of 12.4% (SVP memo, 9 April 2026), against a 13.5% target.","locator":"Where we are today"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-cffaa0f1","quote":"period: 2025-Q2
metric: search_to_cart_rate
value: 12.4","locator":"search metrics row 5"},"summary":"Both statements can be true at different times. 12.4% is a real value in the series, but for 2025-Q2; the roadmap presents it under 'Where we are today' (drafted 2026-05-21) and the SVP memo of 2026-04-09 states it as the current level. The decline from 12.4% to 10.7% across the intervening quarters is not reflected in either document.","how_to_resolve":"Date-stamp every conversion figure in the memo, roadmap and slides to its source period. metric: zero_result_rate
value: 3.0","locator":"search metrics row 8"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-465d6868","quote":"period: 2026-Q2
metric: zero_result_rate_submitted_only
value: 9.2","locator":"search metrics row 13"},"summary":"Two zero-result rates exist for 2026-Q2. value: 8.6","locator":"search metrics row 10; compare EV-465d6868 at 9.2 for 2026-Q2 on the same definition"},"summary":"The 2025-Q4 headline figure of 8.6% was computed on typed-and-submitted queries only, the same basis as the 2026-Q2 restated figure of 9.2%. search_count: 38412
cause_category: synonym_gap
catalogue_status: stocked as drywall panel","locator":"zero result queries row 1"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-8c6f532a","quote":"Those eighteen terms account for 7.3% of zero-result search volume in the quarter. Synonym gap is the leading assigned cause within the eighteen hand-reviewed head terms; those terms are only 7.3% of zero-result volume. search_count: 17250
cause_category: not_stocked
catalogue_status: discontinued 2025-Q3 with no substitute mapped","locator":"zero result queries row 7"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-76865d91","quote":"query_term: house wire 12 2
search_count: 21663
cause_category: attribute_query

metric: search_session_share
value: 11.0
unit: percent
segment: trade_account","locator":"search metrics row 25"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-8873548a","quote":"period: 2026-Q2
metric: search_revenue_share
value: 34.0
unit: percent
segment: trade_account","locator":"search metrics row 26"},"summary":"Both true of the same segment measured two ways. Trade is 11% of search sessions but 34% of search-originated revenue, with a restated zero-result rate of 16.4% against consumer 8.3% and search-to-cart of 7.9% against consumer 11.0%. Prioritising by session volume points away from trade; prioritising by revenue exposure points at it.","how_to_resolve":"Decide whether the objective is weighted by sessions or by revenue. Sizing the recoverable revenue behind the 16.4% trade zero-result rate would settle which segment the intervention should target."},{"id":"C14","topic":"Interview evidence on abandonment: strength vs recruitment bias","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-8c6f532a","quote":"Nine trade customers were interviewed. UX research itself asks that it be treated as a hypothesis and not a number.","how_to_resolve":"Re-recruit from digital-only trade accounts and from sessions that ended at a zero-result page, then re-measure abandonment."},{"id":"C15","topic":"Synonym pilot conversion lift: measured movement vs unattributable to the change","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-8c6f532a","quote":"Search-to-cart conversion on that storefront moved from 11.8% in the four weeks before the pilot to 12.3% during it.","locator":"Synonym mapping pilot — secondary storefront"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-8c6f532a","quote":"There was no holdout group. The pilot ran across the holiday trading peak, when search-to-cart conversion rises on both storefronts every year. The conversion movement cannot be separated from the season.","locator":"Synonym mapping pilot — secondary storefront"},"summary":"The synonym pilot's headline conversion gain of 0.5pp and its own invalidation appear in the same record. The zero-result reduction for the 120 mapped terms (100% to 3.2%) is a direct measurement of the mechanism; the conversion figure is confounded by holiday seasonality with no holdout.","how_to_resolve":"Re-run synonym expansion on the primary storefront with a randomised holdout outside the trading peak. Synonym updates are exempt from the code freeze, so this can run during Q4."},{"id":"C16","topic":"Deliverability of the ranking re-platform inside H2","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-843a50ab","quote":"Approve the ranking re-platform for delivery in H2 2026. Platform engineering states the work is unestimated and needs infrastructure not currently operated; the roadmap's own open items say effort is not estimated and a discovery spike is requested before any date is committed. The storefront code freeze from 2026-10-15 to 2027-01-05 also removes most of H2's remaining shipping window.","how_to_resolve":"Complete Nadia's two-week discovery spike and produce an estimate, then test it against the freeze window and the FY26 platform spend cap before any delivery date is approved."},{"id":"C17","topic":"Ranking approach vs governance and merchandising requirements","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-7ad64618","quote":"I am asking the Search and Discovery team to plan a ranking re-platform for H2 — learned ranking over a vector index — with a recommendation ready for the August planning review.","locator":"What I want"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-bdf52db3","quote":"Any automated system that determines which products a customer is shown must carry a documented description of its ranking factors, reviewable by merchandising on request. This applies to learned ranking models and there is no exemption for model complexity.","locator":"Automated ranking transparency"},"summary":"The requested intervention is a learned ranking model. Governance requires documented, merchandising-reviewable ranking factors with no complexity exemption, requires manual pin and demote overrides to be preserved, and caps personalised ranking at 22% consent coverage. Neither the memo nor the slides addresses these constraints.","how_to_resolve":"Have legal-privacy review the proposed architecture against the transparency, override and consent requirements before the August decision, and confirm whether any new vendor triggers the eight-to-ten-week assessment."},{"id":"C18","topic":"Vendor conversion-lift claim vs internal measurement capability","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-843a50ab","quote":"Thurlow Discovery Labs reports a 22% lift in search conversion for retail clients after deploying its ranking service.","locator":"Slide 6 — Market"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-16f9f013","quote":"synthetic - never populated; no human relevance judgement set exists and no query has ever been scored for relevance","locator":"search metrics row 27"},"summary":"A vendor-reported 22% conversion lift is offered as market evidence for ranking. Internally there is no relevance judgement set, no online ranking A/B test and no measurement of ranking quality, so the organisation has no baseline against which a vendor lift could be verified or replicated. The roadmap concedes there is no measurement of ranking quality to set a target against.","how_to_resolve":"Request the vendor's methodology, baseline and client population, and establish an internal relevance baseline before treating the 22% figure as applicable."},{"id":"C19","topic":"Whether catalogue and attribute work is a viable path","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-7ad64618","quote":"I have not seen a relevance analysis and I do not think we need one to know this. We have spent two years tidying product data and the conversion line has gone backwards.","locator":"What I want"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-aab2655b","quote":"Only 41% of SKUs have structured size or dimension attributes populated. Attribute-filtered search cannot be built on the current data.","locator":"Catalogue data"},"summary":"The memo dismisses catalogue work on the grounds that two years of it coincided with falling conversion. Platform engineering records that structured attributes are populated for only 41% of SKUs, and three of the eighteen head zero-result terms are attribute queries against unsearchable fields — so the catalogue data is not in a state where the attribute path has been tried and failed.","how_to_resolve":"Separate 'catalogue tidying already done' from 'attribute coverage still missing'. Establish what share of zero-result volume is attribute-driven before ruling the catalogue path out."},{"id":"C20","topic":"Synonym expansion below the line vs synonym gap as leading categorised cause","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-a2654f30","quote":"| 2 | Synonym dictionary expansion | catalogue operations | continues at current staffing, below the line |","locator":"H2 candidates"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-38366396","quote":"The synonym file is a flat file maintained by two people. The backlog is 1,900 unmapped terms and it grows faster than we clear it.","locator":"Round the room — Dev Achterberg"},"summary":"The roadmap holds synonym expansion below the line at current staffing because it does not act on ranking. Catalogue operations states that at current staffing the 1,900-term backlog grows faster than it is cleared, so 'continues at current staffing' means the gap widens. Synonym gap is meanwhile the most frequent assigned cause among the eighteen categorised head terms, and synonym updates are exempt from the Q4 code freeze.","how_to_resolve":"Cost the throughput needed to clear the backlog and model the zero-result reduction against the 9.2% restated rate, then compare that against the unestimated re-platform on the same basis."}]}

search_relevance_mandate::missing_eviden.text: {"gaps":[{"id":"GAP-001","question":"How good or bad is current ranking quality — i.e. for searches that do return results, how often does the customer reach a relevant product?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"The entire case for the ranking re-platform rests on ranking being the primary driver of poor findability, but no relevance measurement exists anywhere. The relevance_judged_queries field is present in the metrics set and was never populated, and analytics states explicitly that every findability measure published is a measure of searches that returned nothing. Without any measurement of ignored-but-non-empty results, the ranking hypothesis is unmeasured and unfalsified, and the alternative (coverage/synonym/spell/attribute gaps) has the only quantified evidence. A half-year commitment would be made to an untested premise.","how_to_obtain":"Build a human-judged relevance set: sample stratified queries from the restated typed-and-submitted series, have merchandising and catalogue operations rate top-10 results per query, and compute a baseline relevance metric. Also instrument result-set abandonment (searches returning results with no click or no cart add). Both are pre-work, not a re-platform.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-002","question":"What is the engineering effort, elapsed time and cost of the ranking re-platform (embedding 1.2M SKUs, standing up a GPU serving tier)?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"No figure has ever been produced — the roadmap records the estimate as open and platform engineering states the work has not been estimated. Platform spend is capped at the FY26 approved figure with no net new headcount, so a candidate whose cost is unknown cannot be shown to fit inside the limit, and cannot be shown to land before the 2026-10-15 storefront code freeze. A large number would make the option infeasible this half-year regardless of its merits.","how_to_obtain":"Complete the two-week discovery spike already actioned to Nadia Fenwick and require a costed estimate (build effort, GPU serving run-rate, embedding pipeline cost) before the August planning review.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-003","question":"What are the causes of the remaining 92.7% of zero-result search volume that has never been categorised?","impact":"would_change_scope","why_it_matters":"Hand review covered only the eighteen highest-volume terms, which account for 7.3% of zero-result volume in 2026-Q2. Nothing is known about whether the tail resembles the head. The synonym-versus-misspelling-versus-not-stocked-versus-attribute mix in the tail determines which fix retires the most of the 4.11 million quarterly zero-result searches, and whether synonym mapping (a data change, freeze-exempt) or spell correction (code, freeze-bound) is the larger lever.","how_to_obtain":"Sample the zero-result tail (e.g. a random 300–500 terms weighted by volume) and apply the same cause taxonomy; report volume-weighted cause shares with confidence intervals.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-004","question":"What is the causal effect of synonym mapping on search-to-cart conversion, isolated from seasonality?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"The secondary-storefront pilot ran with no holdout across the holiday trading peak, so the 11.8%→12.3% conversion movement cannot be separated from the season. The pilot measured its zero-result effect on mapped terms but could not measure its own conversion effect. Treating that 0.5pp as a synonym benefit would overstate the alternative; treating it as zero would understate it. Either way the size of the recommended intervention's payoff is unquantified.","how_to_obtain":"Run a query-level or geo/storefront-randomised holdout on the next synonym batch on the primary storefront, outside a trading peak, with search-to-cart as the primary metric.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-005","question":"What throughput can catalogue operations achieve on the synonym backlog, and how many of the 1,900 unmapped terms clear per week or month?","impact":"would_change_scope","why_it_matters":"Synonym expansion is the freeze-exempt, in-budget candidate, but no volume or effort figure exists: we know two people maintain a flat file and the backlog grows faster than it is cleared, but no terms-per-week rate, no cost per mapped term, and no coverage curve against zero-result volume. Without it the team cannot size how much of the 4.11M quarterly zero-result searches a prioritised mapping push would retire by the end of FY26, nor whether it needs tooling rather than more hands.","how_to_obtain":"Ask catalogue operations for historical mapping throughput from the pipeline deploy logs and the November–December pilot (120 terms over six weeks), plus an estimate of effort per term at head versus tail volume.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-006","question":"What share of search sessions and search-originated revenue do trade accounts represent by zero-result exposure, and what happens to trade sessions after a zero result?","impact":"would_change_scope","why_it_matters":"There is a segment breakdown by account type for zero-result rate and search-to-cart (trade 16.4% and 7.9% against consumer 8.3% and 11.0%), but no breakdown of zero-result causes by segment, and no session-level outcome data for trade after failure. Trade is 11% of sessions and 34% of search revenue, so whether trade failures are synonym gaps (trade terminology), not-stocked/channel-only items, or attribute queries determines which intervention protects the highest-value segment. Cause categorisation exists along the volume dimension only, never along the segment dimension.","how_to_obtain":"Re-cut the zero-result cause categorisation split by account_type; join zero-result events to subsequent session behaviour within the 180-day retention window.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-007","question":"How many customers abandon after a zero result, and what revenue is lost — as opposed to what a small self-selected feedback sample says?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"The abandonment claim rests on nine trade interviews recruited at two trade counters (all already in-store shoppers) and on a feedback survey whose link appears only on zero-result pages. Both instruments are structurally incapable of measuring rate or value, and both exclude the population that matters most: customers who search, get results, and leave. No behavioural quantification of abandonment or lost revenue exists.","how_to_obtain":"Session-level analysis of exit and re-query behaviour after zero-result and after non-empty-but-unclicked searches; attach basket value of recovered sessions to estimate revenue at stake.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-008","question":"Is there any evidence at all about consumer and guest customers who do not fail — i.e. the ~89% of sessions that are not trade and the searches that return results?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"Every qualitative source is conditioned on failure: interviews recruited from trade counters, feedback triggered only on zero-result pages. No source in the pack observes a successful or mediocre-but-non-empty search from any segment. The desired outcome is framed as the share of sessions reaching a relevant product, and that population has no evidence of any kind. If most lost value sits in poor-but-non-empty result sets, both the synonym and the ranking case are being argued from the wrong sample.","how_to_obtain":"Add a post-search survey trigger on result-bearing pages, and run moderated usability sessions with consumer and guest participants recruited outside stores.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-009","question":"How much of the 400 ms p95 latency budget would a re-ranking stage consume?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"Platform engineering states the current index averages 180 ms and that nobody has measured the re-ranking cost. If a learned ranking stage plus vector retrieval breaches the p95 requirement, the primary bet fails a hard platform constraint independent of its relevance benefit.","how_to_obtain":"Bench the February learning-to-rank prototype and a candidate vector retrieval path under production-like query load; report p95 added latency.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-010","question":"Can a learned ranking model satisfy the automated ranking transparency requirement, preserve merchandising pin and demote, and operate within data residency and the 22% consent ceiling — and has any assessment been started?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"Governance imposes documented ranking-factor descriptions with no exemption for model complexity, mandatory manual override, regional confinement of query logs, and consent for identity-varying ranking at only 22% coverage; a new vendor needs an 8–10 week assessment. No legal review of the proposed re-platform against any of these appears in the pack, and no assessment is recorded as begun. If the design cannot meet transparency or override, or if a vendor path adds ten weeks against a 2026-10-15 freeze, the recommendation changes.","how_to_obtain":"Request a written pre-assessment from legal-privacy against the re-platform design and, if the Thurlow vendor is in scope, initiate the data protection assessment immediately to expose the true start date.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-011","question":"Is the reported 22% conversion lift from the vendor's ranking service applicable to this catalogue, engine and customer mix — and what is the underlying methodology and baseline?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"The market slide cites a single vendor's self-reported figure with no client set, no baseline, no comparison design and no independent verification. It is currently the only quantified benefit estimate attached to the primary bet, so its unexamined status directly inflates confidence in the recommendation.","how_to_obtain":"Request the vendor's methodology, client sample and reference calls; discount to a defensible internal range or exclude the figure until an internal A/B can produce one.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-012","question":"Is the leadership consensus on ranking based on independent evidence, or on a single source restated three times?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"The review slides present three converging workstreams, but the pack's own appendix shows the roadmap cites the SVP memo and the standup cites the roadmap; the memo itself rests on personal phone use, three store manager conversations and an explicit statement that no relevance analysis was seen. There is no independent analytical source for the ranking diagnosis, and the one recorded dissent is from the engineer closest to the data. What is missing is any evidence that the consensus adds information.","how_to_obtain":"Ask each cited workstream to state its primary evidence; treat the diagnosis as one unverified hypothesis until GAP-001 produces a measurement.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-013","question":"What is the position-bias-corrected estimate of the learning-to-rank prototype's online effect?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"The February offline evaluation reported NDCG@10 +0.06, but it was trained and evaluated on uncorrected click logs from the incumbent ranker, so it rewards reproducing the existing ordering; the prototype has never been served to a customer. The +0.06 is therefore not an effect estimate at all, and no online number exists to replace it. Deciding as if it were evidence of gain is the main risk to support level.","how_to_obtain":"Collect randomised-interleaving or small-exposure position data to estimate propensities, re-evaluate with inverse-propensity weighting, and if promising run a bounded online A/B before committing the half-year.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-014","question":"What would it cost and take to backfill structured size and dimension attributes for the 59% of SKUs that lack them, and who owns the merchandising dependency?","impact":"would_change_scope","why_it_matters":"Attribute queries appear three times in the categorised zero-result head and repeatedly in feedback, yet attribute-filtered search is blocked because only 41% of SKUs have the data. The candidate sits below the line as merchandising-dependent with no effort, cost or timeline figure, so its true position against the other options has never been tested.","how_to_obtain":"Ask catalogue operations and merchandising for a scoped backfill estimate for the top categories by attribute-query volume, rather than for the full catalogue.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-015","question":"What is the effort and expected coverage of spell correction and fuzzy matching, and can it ship before the 2026-10-15 code freeze?","impact":"would_change_scope","why_it_matters":"Two of the eighteen categorised head terms are misspellings with no fuzzy matching configured, and feedback names mistyping directly, but the candidate is recorded as not scoped with no estimate at all. Because it is storefront code it is freeze-bound, so an unscoped item cannot be sequenced. Its absence may be hiding a cheap, quantifiable win.","how_to_obtain":"Time-box a scoping estimate from search platform engineering, sized against the misspelling share established by the tail sample in GAP-003.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-016","question":"How much of the zero-result volume is genuinely not stocked, and what is the intended commercial response?","impact":"would_change_scope","why_it_matters":"Three of the eighteen head terms are not_stocked — discontinued with no substitute, special-order-only, or trade-counter-channel-only — totalling substantial volume that no search intervention can fix. No assortment, substitution-mapping or listing decision is recorded anywhere, and no owner is named. Scoping a search fix over demand that requires a catalogue or channel decision would misallocate the half-year.","how_to_obtain":"Route the not_stocked terms to merchandising for an explicit list-or-substitute decision, and quantify their share of total zero-result volume via the tail sample.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-017","question":"What is the restated, definition-consistent zero-result and search-to-cart series by segment across enough periods to establish a trend?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"Segment splits for trade and consumer exist for 2026-Q2 only; there is no prior-period segment series, so it is impossible to say whether the trade gap is widening or stable. Meanwhile the review slides' central trend claim — that zero-result rate halved and coverage is no longer the constraint — uses the non-comparable headline series, whereas the restated series shows the rate rising from 8.6% to 9.2%. search_relevance_mandate::recommendation.text: {"recommendation":{"statement":"Prioritise OPT-04: resource synonym dictionary expansion against the zero-result tail and ship it as a randomised, term-level holdout (switchback) rollout — and fund OPT-03 (relevance judgement set plus instrumentation of non-zero-result failure) alongside it as the gate on any ranking bet. search_relevance_mandate::challenger::v1.text: {"findings":[{"question":"claims_supported","verdict":"concern","explanation":"Most claims are accurately sourced, but three problems: (1) C6 states consumer search-to-cart of 11.0% and cites EV-8873548a, which is trade revenue share, not consumer conversion — the 11.0% consumer figure lives in a different record and is not among the cited ids (note 11.0 is also the trade session-share value, so the coincidence invites confusion). (2) The volume claim is inflated in framing. The ten synonym-gap head terms total ~198,700 searches, i.e. roughly 4.8% of the 4.11m zero-result population and about 0.4pp of the 9.2% restated rate — 'hundreds of thousands of searches a quarter' is at the very edge of the arithmetic, and the recommendation never states that the directly-evidenced scope cannot approach the sub-5% zero-result objective. (3) The pilot evidence is weaker at group scale than the summary implies: storefront-wide zero-result fell only 0.9pp on a storefront carrying ~8% of group volume, and that fact is not carried into the support statement alongside the 100%-to-3.2% figure.","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-8873548a","quote":"synthetic - trade accounts as a share of search-originated revenue"},{"evidence_id":"EV-b1dce1aa","quote":"synthetic - consumer accounts and guests"},{"evidence_id":"EV-e08924b9","quote":"search_count: 38412"},{"evidence_id":"EV-78f74943","quote":"value: 4.11"},{"evidence_id":"EV-a2654f30","quote":"Bring the zero-result rate below 5%."},{"evidence_id":"EV-8c6f532a","quote":"That storefront carries roughly 8% of group search volume, so the pilot does not move the group figures reported by analytics."},{"evidence_id":"EV-8c6f532a","quote":"Storefront-wide zero-result rate fell by 0.9 percentage points."}]},{"question":"contradictions_considered","verdict":"concern","explanation":"The metric and provenance conflicts (12.4% vs 10.7%, 3.0% vs 9.2%, the single-source 'convergence', the recorded dissent, the circular NDCG) are engaged directly and well. One substantive contradiction is disposed of as preference rather than answered: the SVP's argument is not only 'ranking feels wrong', it is that two years of catalogue data work coincided with a falling conversion line. The recommendation's own C12/C4 evidence shows search-to-cart declining every quarter for five quarters while catalogue operations were clearing the synonym backlog at current staffing — that is a prima facie counter-signal to prioritising more of the same work, and it is used only to argue against no-change, never against OPT-04. The draft's rebuttal (C14) rebuts the memo's authority, not its correlation.","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-7ad64618","quote":"We have spent two years tidying product data and the conversion line has gone backwards."},{"evidence_id":"EV-f95c4db3","quote":"value: 10.7"},{"evidence_id":"EV-38366396","quote":"Dev: continue clearing the synonym backlog at current pace."}]},{"question":"preference_as_evidence","verdict":"concern","explanation":"The draft is disciplined about OPT-11's backing being senior preference. It is less disciplined about the preferences that favour its own choice. C9 is labelled a business_constraint, but the operative numbers — two maintainers, 1,900 unmapped terms, 'grows faster than we clear it' — are a single verbal report in a standup whose own header states these are statements, not findings; the draft elsewhere concedes throughput has never been measured, yet the backlog-growth assertion is carried into the recommendation as a constraint. Similarly, 'terminology failure is concentrated in trade' is an inference from a feedback corpus collected only on zero-result pages plus a nine-person counter-recruited sample; the trade 16.4% zero-result rate is a fact, but that it is caused by vocabulary rather than coverage or misspelling is not.","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-38366396","quote":"These are notes of what people said in a fifteen-minute standup. They are statements, not findings."},{"evidence_id":"EV-38366396","quote":"The backlog is 1,900 unmapped terms and it grows faster than we clear it."},{"evidence_id":"EV-4c3f0208","quote":"synthetic - survey link appears only on a search page that returned no results"}]},{"question":"non_ai_considered","verdict":"concern","explanation":"Non-AI options are argued at length and one is selected, so this is not a box-tick. The flaw is in how the other non-AI options are deferred. The recommendation says to re-open OPT-05 (spell correction), OPT-07 (not-stocked) and OPT-08 (zero-result page) only 'once the tail categorisation exists', while also recording that anything with a storefront element must land before 2026-10-15. subscription_churn::contradictions::v2.text: {"contradictions":[{"id":"C1","topic":"Direction of monthly churn and whether the FY26 target trend is holding","kind":"temporal_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-07d95016","quote":"Monthly churn improved to 6.9% in Q1 after two quarters of increase, and the FY26 target of 5.5% remains achievable if the trend holds.","locator":"retention_objectives.md, Current position (doc updated 2026-02-10)"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-7b8b9849","quote":"value: 7.2","locator":"subscriber_metrics.csv row 1: period 2026-Q2, metric monthly_churn_rate, segment all (updated 2026-07-15)"},"summary":"The strategy document's 6.9% is the 2026-Q1 figure and is stale rather than wrong: the same series shows 7.2% for 2026-Q2, i.e. churn rose again after the quoted improvement. Any statement that 'the trend holds' belongs to the Q1 vintage of the data.","how_to_resolve":"Re-state the current position against the latest subscriber_metrics.csv period (2026-Q2 = 7.2%) and confirm with analytics whether Q2 is final or partial; then re-test whether 5.5% by end-FY26 is still reachable."},{"id":"C2","topic":"What the largest single cause of cancellation is","kind":"scope_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-99848be3","quote":"Recipe variety is the dominant reason subscribers give for leaving. It accounts for 41.6% of coded responses, more than twice the next category.","locator":"exit_survey_analysis.md, Headline finding"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-1f575ec3","quote":"share_of_cancellations_percent: 47.2","locator":"cancellation_breakdown.csv row 1: 2026-Q2, channel = payment_lapse, exit_survey_offered: no"},"summary":"Both 'largest cause' claims can be true of different segments. Recipe variety is the largest cause among the 214 subscribers who completed the exit survey — a survey only reachable inside the account-page flow, which is 34.1% of cancellations (EV-f6de8737). Payment lapse is the largest cancellation channel overall at 47.2%, and that group is never offered the survey, so it cannot appear in the reason shares at all.","how_to_resolve":"State the denominator with each figure: 'largest stated reason among account-page cancellers' vs 'largest cancellation channel overall'. To compare like with like, instrument the payment-lapse path and obtain the share of payment-lapse cancellations that self-recover within 30 days — the figure the finance partner asked for and nobody had (EV-ec6d1455)."},{"id":"C3","topic":"Whether the expanded-menu pilot moved retention","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-ec6d1455","quote":"And the menu pilot did move retention. I saw the numbers.","locator":"stakeholder_notes.md, Head of Culinary — Owen Baptiste"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-2b7ae6db","quote":"Day-90 retention was 71.2% in the test arm against 70.4% in the control arm, with 1,900 subscribers per arm. The difference is not statistically meaningful.","locator":"prior_experiments.md, Expanded menu pilot (February–April 2026)"},"summary":"The Head of Culinary reports the pilot moved retention; the experiment record reports a 0.8pp gap at n=1,900 per arm that is not statistically meaningful. Both refer to the same February–April 2026 pilot.","how_to_resolve":"Ask the Head of Culinary which readout he saw (arm, metric, window) and have research publish the confidence interval and powering for the 71.2% vs 70.4% comparison."},{"id":"C4","topic":"Whether the expanded-menu result bears on the cohort that is actually churning","kind":"scope_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-2b7ae6db","quote":"The pilot excluded subscribers in their first 30 days by design, so as not to disturb the onboarding sequence.","locator":"prior_experiments.md, Expanded menu pilot"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-cbdcb46d","quote":"value: 62.4","locator":"subscriber_metrics.csv row 10: 2026-Q2, share_of_cancellations_within_21_days, segment all"},"summary":"The only menu-breadth evidence covers subscribers past day 30, while 62.4% of 2026-Q2 cancellations occur within 21 days. The pilot and the churn mass describe different populations, so the null result neither supports nor rules out menu breadth for early-tenure subscribers.","how_to_resolve":"Run or model a menu-breadth arm that includes the first 30 days — noting the same document records that no test has measured whether menu breadth affects subscribers in their first month — or cross-tabulate exit-survey reason against tenure, which EV-99848be3 states has never been done."},{"id":"C5","topic":"Whether the Q1 churn improvement is real or an artefact of the definition change","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-ec6d1455","quote":"Churn turned the corner in Q1. We just have to hold the line while acquisition scales.","locator":"stakeholder_notes.md, Growth Lead — Priya Ramanathan"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-3451c727","quote":"from 2026-01-01, subscribers who pause are reported as active rather than as cancellations.","locator":"prior_decisions.md, FIN-2025-19"},"summary":"The Q1 fall from 7.6% (EV-ab95f994, 'prior definition - paused subscribers were counted as cancellations') to 6.9% (EV-eb6216ce, 'definition changed on 2026-01-01') coincides exactly with the reporting change, and 61.0% of the 2026-Q1 paused cohort cancelled within 90 days anyway (EV-215b7dd7). The claimed turning point may be definitional rather than behavioural.","how_to_resolve":"Ask analytics to restate 2026-Q1 and 2026-Q2 churn under the pre-2026 definition (pauses counted as cancellations) and compare the two series on a like-for-like basis."},{"id":"C6","topic":"Delivery reliability: network figure versus the sites that serve first boxes","kind":"scope_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-74a9cee5","quote":"Network on-time delivery was 96.2% in 2026-Q2, comfortably above the 95% service standard.","locator":"fulfilment_report.md, On-time delivery"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-74a9cee5","quote":"Ashby opened in January 2026 and is still ramping. New subscribers are routed to Ashby by default while the site builds volume, and Ashby handled 71% of first boxes in 2026-Q2.","locator":"fulfilment_report.md, On-time delivery (Ashby 88.7%)"},"summary":"Both are true of different populations. The 96.2% network figure is volume-weighted across all boxes and passes the standard; the site that handles 71% of first boxes runs at 88.7%, below the standard. The report also states first-box performance has never been reported separately from the network figure.","how_to_resolve":"Have operations publish on-time delivery for first boxes specifically, split by site, so the new-subscriber experience can be judged against the 95% standard."},{"id":"C7","topic":"How much delivery problems matter to churn","kind":"scope_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-99848be3","quote":"Delivery and packaging complaints are comparatively rare at 8.4%.","locator":"exit_survey_analysis.md, Headline finding"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-8838d08d","quote":"subscriber reported a late damaged or incomplete first box - synthetic","locator":"subscriber_metrics.csv row 19: 2026-Q2, first_delivery_issue_reported, value: 11.4, segment cancelled_within_7_days"},"summary":"The survey's 8.4% is pooled across all tenures and drawn only from account-page cancellers. The operational metric shows first-delivery issues reported by 11.4% of those who cancelled within 7 days against 4.3% of those retained at day 90 (EV-bfe90214) — a 2.7x difference concentrated in the earliest cohort that the pooled survey share cannot reveal.","how_to_resolve":"Cross-tabulate exit-survey reason category by tenure at cancellation (the export holds tenure for every respondent but the fields have never been crossed), and compare against first_delivery_issue_reported by cohort."},{"id":"C8","topic":"Restoring a 20-recipe menu versus fulfilment capacity","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-ec6d1455","quote":"The survey could not be clearer. People leave because the food gets boring. Give me back the twenty-recipe menu and this problem goes away.","locator":"stakeholder_notes.md, Head of Culinary — Owen Baptiste"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-74a9cee5","quote":"Ashby cannot support more than 18 weekly recipes before a second pick line is commissioned.","locator":"fulfilment_report.md, Capacity"},"summary":"The proposed intervention (20 weekly recipes) exceeds the stated capacity ceiling at the site handling 71% of first boxes, with the second pick line not scheduled until Q1 2027.","how_to_resolve":"Confirm with operations whether a 20-recipe menu could be served from Rowan and Pell only, or whether commissioning at Ashby can be pulled forward; otherwise cap any menu-breadth pilot at 18 recipes."},{"id":"C9","topic":"Waste rationale for the 2025 menu reduction","kind":"temporal_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-3451c727","quote":"food waste ran at 9.4% of ingredient cost under forecast-to-order sourcing","locator":"prior_decisions.md, OPS-2025-11 (decision dated 2025-09-18)"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-74a9cee5","quote":"Waste has run at 4.1% of ingredient cost since the committed-volume sourcing agreement began in February 2026.","locator":"fulfilment_report.md, Ingredient cost and waste"},"summary":"Both figures are correct for their periods. The 9.4% that justified cutting the menu from 20 to 14 recipes describes the pre-February-2026 forecast-to-order regime; under the current committed-volume agreement waste is 4.1%, so the original rationale may no longer apply.","how_to_resolve":"Ask operations whether the 4.1% figure would hold at a larger recipe count under committed-volume sourcing, and whether the picking-error concern cited in OPS-2025-11 has also changed."},{"id":"C10","topic":"Protecting the 50% first-box offer","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-ec6d1455","quote":"The 50% first-box offer is the best-performing lever we have and I would not touch it.","locator":"stakeholder_notes.md, Growth Lead — Priya Ramanathan"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-2b7ae6db","quote":"The 50% offer acquired 34% more subscribers per unit of acquisition spend. Day-21 retention was 71.9% for the 50% arm and 78.3% for the 30% arm.","locator":"prior_experiments.md, First-box discount depth test (June–August 2025)"},"summary":"The offer is best-performing on acquisition efficiency and worse-performing on day-21 retention (71.9% vs 78.3%) — the metric the churn programme is judged on. The same record notes cost per retained subscriber at day 90 was never calculated for either arm, so neither side has the deciding number.","how_to_resolve":"Calculate cost per retained subscriber at day 90 for both discount arms; note that promotional depth on the first box is owned by growth and out of scope for the retention programme (EV-07d95016)."},{"id":"C11","topic":"Shipping the AI menu recommender before the autumn campaign","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-ec6d1455","quote":"I want the AI menu recommender live before the autumn campaign. Personalisation is how this category is being won and we are the last ones without it.","locator":"stakeholder_notes.md, Chief Marketing Officer — Delia Marchetti"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-429358ce","quote":"Recipe descriptions and menu recommendations generated by a model and shown to a subscriber require human review before publication. This applies regardless of the model's stated confidence and has no volume exemption.","locator":"governance_requirements.md, AI-generated content"},"summary":"The requested launch conflicts with a standing governance requirement for human review of every model-generated recommendation shown to a subscriber, with no volume exemption; a new vendor would additionally need a data protection assessment taking five to seven weeks.","how_to_resolve":"Get legal-privacy to state whether a per-subscriber recommender can satisfy human review at volume, and start the vendor assessment clock; also require the vendor to supply baseline, window and randomisation for the claimed retention lift, which the deck omits."},{"id":"C12","topic":"Where in tenure cancellations occur","kind":"temporal_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-56ffaa2c","quote":"value: 48.1","locator":"subscriber_metrics.csv row 11: 2025-Q2, share_of_cancellations_within_21_days, segment all"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-cbdcb46d","quote":"value: 62.4","locator":"subscriber_metrics.csv row 10: 2026-Q2, share_of_cancellations_within_21_days, segment all"},"summary":"Both are correct for their periods: early-tenure cancellation rose from 48.1% of cancellations in 2025-Q2 to 62.4% in 2026-Q2, alongside median tenure at cancellation falling from 34 days (EV-176eac8a) to 19 days (EV-6e95ea26). Quoting the older share would understate how far churn has shifted into the first three weeks.","how_to_resolve":"Fix 2026-Q2 as the reference period for any prioritisation, and confirm with analytics that the definition change of 2026-01-01 does not affect this tenure series."}]}
