support_ticket_routing::contradictions::.text: {"contradictions":[{"id":"C1","topic":"Current routing accuracy: 78% in the FY26 objectives vs 71% in the metrics series","kind":"metric_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-68cdd2b1","quote":"Routing accuracy sits at 78%.","locator":"support_objectives.md, Current position"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-ac5740e1","quote":"value: 71.2","locator":"routing_metrics.csv row 5, period 2026-Q1, metric routing_accuracy_queue_level"},"summary":"The strategy document's headline accuracy figure (78%) is stale and belongs to a retired definition and an older period: it matches the 2025-Q1 department-level row, not the current queue-level series, which reads 71.2% for 2026-Q1 and 71.4% for 2026-Q2. Support analytics states explicitly that the 78% figure still circulating in planning documents is the 2025-Q1 department-level number (EV-3e2d12e8: \"The 78% figure that still circulates in planning documents is the 2025-Q1 department-level number\").","how_to_resolve":"Have product-leadership restate the FY26 baseline using the queue-level metric name from routing_metrics.csv and the period it was measured in (2026-Q1 = 71.2%, 2026-Q2 = 71.4%), and mark the 78% figure as 2025-Q1 department-level."},{"id":"C2","topic":"Whether pre- and post-April-2025 routing accuracy figures are comparable","kind":"scope_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-db957a15","quote":"note: definition retired 2025-04-01 - department level - not comparable with queue level figures - synthetic","locator":"routing_metrics.csv row 1, period 2025-Q1"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-3e2d12e8","quote":"Under the old definition a ticket counted as correctly routed if it reached the correct department, of which there were three. Under the current definition it counts as correctly routed only if it reached the correct queue, of which there are five.","locator":"data_tooling_notes.md, Routing accuracy definition change"},"summary":"Both records describe the same fact from different sides: the 78.2% figure measures a three-department taxonomy, the 71.x% figures measure a five-queue taxonomy. Any narrative of accuracy 'falling from 78% to 71%' is comparing two different populations of routing decisions, not a regression.","how_to_resolve":"Restate any trend line using only routing_accuracy_queue_level rows (2025-Q2 onward). If a pre-2025-Q2 queue-level number is needed, ask support-analytics whether historical tickets can be re-scored under the five-queue definition."},{"id":"C3","topic":"Median time-to-resolution baseline: 21 hours vs 22.0 / 22.6 hours","kind":"temporal_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-68cdd2b1","quote":"Reduce median time-to-resolution for customer support tickets from 21 hours to 12 hours by the end of FY26.","locator":"support_objectives.md, Annual goals (document updated 2026-01-20)"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-133fecfa","quote":"value: 22.6","locator":"routing_metrics.csv row 11, period 2026-Q2, metric median_time_to_resolution_hours"},"summary":"The '21 hours' baseline in the objectives corresponds to the 2025-Q4 reading (EV-ff35851f: \"value: 21.2\"), the latest available when the document was written in January 2026. The series has since moved the other way: 22.0 hours in 2026-Q1 and 22.6 hours in 2026-Q2. Both figures are true of their own quarter; the goal gap is now 10.6 hours, not 9.","how_to_resolve":"Re-baseline the FY26 goal against the most recent quarter in routing_metrics.csv and state the period alongside the number."},{"id":"C4","topic":"Whether reported median time-to-resolution measures how long customers actually waited","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-428cdc6c","quote":"value: 22.0","locator":"routing_metrics.csv row 10, period 2026-Q1, metric median_time_to_resolution_hours"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-3e2d12e8","quote":"A reopened issue contributes two resolution times, each shorter than the elapsed time the customer actually waited.","locator":"data_tooling_notes.md, Reopen behaviour in the volume export"},"summary":"The headline time-to-resolution metric is computed per record, and since the Relay 5.2 release each reopened issue produces two records. With 14% of 2026-Q2 tickets reopened within 14 days (EV-71c6137f: \"value: 14.0\"), the published median understates customer-experienced wait by an unquantified amount, so the metric the goal is written against and the quantity the goal cares about are not the same thing.","how_to_resolve":"Ask support-analytics to produce a per-issue time-to-resolution that stitches clone records back to their `reopened_from` original, and compare it with the per-record series for 2025-Q4 through 2026-Q2."},{"id":"C5","topic":"Year-over-year ticket volume growth of 16.7%","kind":"metric_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-68cdd2b1","quote":"Ticket volume is up 16.7% year over year, from 35,900 to 41,880 per quarter.","locator":"support_objectives.md, Current position"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-3e2d12e8","quote":"A year-over-year comparison that uses `exported_rows` across that date is comparing two different things and will overstate growth.","locator":"data_tooling_notes.md, Reopen behaviour in the volume export"},"summary":"The 16.7% figure compares 2025-Q2 exported_rows (35,900, with zero reopen clones per EV-00512857) against 2026-Q2 exported_rows (41,880, of which 5,140 are clones per EV-e8b9716e). On the distinct-issue basis the tooling notes prescribe, 2026-Q2 is 36,740 issues, roughly 2% above 2025-Q2. Delia Okonjo's meeting statement repeats the inflated figure (EV-6404931e: \"Volume is up nearly 17% and we are holding headcount.\").","how_to_resolve":"Recompute the year-over-year comparison as exported_rows minus reopen_rows_included for both quarters, and answer the question raised and not answered in the review: how much of the increase is reopened tickets rather than new ones."},{"id":"C6","topic":"Whether further rules-engine tuning can raise accuracy","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-6404931e","quote":"We have not really invested in the rules engine. Two more tuning passes and we would be at 85%.","locator":"stakeholder_notes.md, Marek Vandal, Head of Support"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-79d2ae90","quote":"Our assessment is that keyword rules have reached their ceiling on this ticket mix.","locator":"routing_engine_history.md, Assessment 2026-06-30"},"summary":"The Head of Support expects roughly +14 points from two more tuning passes; support-engineering's version log shows three expansion passes adding 176 rules moved accuracy 0.6 points in twelve months and expects no different from a fourth. Marek named no specific passes (EV-6404931e records that \"he said the team would work it out\").","how_to_resolve":"Ask Marek for the specific rule families he believes are missing, and have support-engineering score them against the 2026-Q1 held-out set; the rules engine can be replayed offline, as the classifier trial did."},{"id":"C7","topic":"Does adding a model require new ML infrastructure spend in FY26","kind":"temporal_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-68cdd2b1","quote":"standing up dedicated model-serving infrastructure for support was quoted at $180k of capital plus two engineers","locator":"support_objectives.md, D-2025-11 (dated 2025-11-14)"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-ac98dec8","quote":"Adding a third model requires no new infrastructure and no new vendor.","locator":"technical_constraints.md, Model serving"},"summary":"Both were true when written. The FY26 no-ML-spend decision was taken 2025-11-14, before the internal serving platform existed; Modelyard went live 2026-02-09, hosts CPU inference up to 2 GB, and already carries two fulfilment models. The 340 MB trial model with 41 ms median inference fits inside both that limit and the platform's 400 ms routing budget, so the cost premise behind D-2025-11 may no longer hold — but the decision itself has not been revisited in evidence.","how_to_resolve":"Have engineering-leadership re-examine D-2025-11 against the Modelyard cost position, and have data-platform close the trial's open gap: \"We have not estimated the cost of running or retraining this model in production.\""},{"id":"C8","topic":"Does the classifier beat the rules engine — overall vs per queue","kind":"scope_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-8dc73255","quote":"Overall the classifier routed 88.5% of held-out tickets to the correct queue against the rules engine's 71.2%.","locator":"classifier_trial_report.md, Results on the held-out set"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-8dc73255","quote":"In Billing & Payments the rules engine is more accurate: 84.7% against 83.7%.","locator":"classifier_trial_report.md, Results on the held-out set"},"summary":"Both statements are true of different segments. The classifier wins across all 4,800 held-out tickets and in four of five queues, and loses in Billing & Payments, where payment identifiers and card-decline phrasing match keyword rules exactly. A blanket 'replace the rules engine' framing drops the Billing exception; a Billing-first framing drops the overall result.","how_to_resolve":"Decide per queue rather than globally: specify whether Billing & Payments stays on rules while other queues move, and confirm the split holds outside the January–March held-out window, which the report flags as shaped by the post-holiday returns peak."},{"id":"C9","topic":"Which queue is the worst-routed — lowest accuracy vs largest share of misroutes","kind":"scope_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-8dc73255","quote":"| Account & Access | 410 | 237 | 57.8% | 357 | 87.1% |","locator":"classifier_trial_report.md, results table"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-8dc73255","quote":"Technical Faults routed to Orders & Delivery: 214 of 1,382 misroutes (15.5%)","locator":"classifier_trial_report.md, Misroute structure"},"summary":"Two defensible readings of 'the biggest routing problem'. By accuracy rate, Account & Access is worst (57.8%, on only 410 held-out tickets). By volume of misroutes, Technical Faults is worst, and it also carries the slowest resolution time of any queue (EV-dfe0bc2f: \"value: 34.1\", segment technical_faults, 2026-Q2). Each describes a different segment, and prioritising by rate and by volume point at different queues.","how_to_resolve":"State whether the team is optimising misroute rate or total misrouted tickets (and therefore total hours of delay), then rank queues on the chosen measure using 2026-Q2 volumes."},{"id":"C10","topic":"How costly a misroute is: 'agent moves it within the shift' vs 51.8-hour median","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-6404931e","quote":"Asked what happens today when a rule sends a ticket to the wrong place, she said the agent moves it, usually within the same shift.","locator":"stakeholder_notes.md, Ines Bracko"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-8576e42f","quote":"value: 51.8","locator":"routing_metrics.csv row 15, period 2026-Q2, metric median_time_to_resolution_hours, segment misrouted"},"summary":"The Technical Faults team lead describes misroutes as cheap and quickly corrected; the metrics show reassigned tickets resolving in a median of 51.8 hours against 14.2 hours for tickets resolved in their first queue (EV-b7f6b080: \"value: 14.2\"). The gap cannot be attributed to misrouting alone — analytics notes there is no complexity score, so the two segments cannot be compared like for like.","how_to_resolve":"Measure the reassignment timestamp gap directly from routing_decision_log state transitions to test the 'same shift' claim, and note that per EV-3e2d12e8 there is \"no complexity or effort score on tickets\" to control for ticket difficulty."},{"id":"C11","topic":"Whether the classifier's cost is known","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-6404931e","quote":"The classifier will pay for itself inside a quarter.","locator":"stakeholder_notes.md, Tomas Ferreira"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-8dc73255","quote":"We have not estimated the cost of running or retraining this model in production.","locator":"classifier_trial_report.md, Limitations"},"summary":"A payback claim was made in the review; the trial team states no cost estimate exists, and the trial ran on unmetered shared batch capacity. The stakeholder record itself notes \"No cost model was presented and none exists.\"","how_to_resolve":"Require a serving-plus-retraining cost estimate on Modelyard and a stated benefit mechanism before treating payback as an input, given cost per ticket is a board-reported measure this year."},{"id":"C12","topic":"Vendor's 92% routing accuracy vs the in-house trial's 88.5%","kind":"scope_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-6404931e","quote":"routes 92% of tickets correctly out of the box","locator":"stakeholder_notes.md, Vendor briefing (Tessarine AutoTriage)"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-8dc73255","quote":"Overall the classifier routed 88.5% of held-out tickets to the correct queue against the rules engine's 71.2%.","locator":"classifier_trial_report.md, Results on the held-out set"},"summary":"The two numbers are not measured on the same thing: the vendor figure has no stated sample, baseline, queue taxonomy or industry, while 88.5% is measured on 4,800 held-out Norvane tickets under the five-queue definition. They may both be accurate of different populations, and neither is evidence about the other. Separately, the vendor route faces governance friction: Tessarine \"would process ticket text on its own infrastructure\", while policy requires an assessment taking six to eight weeks.","how_to_resolve":"Ask Tessarine for the sample, taxonomy and baseline behind 92%, and confirm with legal-privacy whether in-region processing can be met at all before starting the data protection assessment, since EV-46e54a4b states \"Training or inference outside the region of origin is not permitted.\""},{"id":"C13","topic":"Manual triage desk: best measured accuracy vs frozen headcount","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-06ff9877","quote":"At that rate, covering every intake stream at current arrival volume would take about five full-time routers.","locator":"prior_experiments.md, Manual triage desk pilot"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-68cdd2b1","quote":"Support headcount is frozen for FY26.","locator":"support_objectives.md, Priorities and constraints"},"summary":"Hand routing produced the highest accuracy any intervention has shown (94.0% against 61.8% for the rules engine on comparable tickets), but scaling it needs about five FTEs against a frozen headcount and a flat cost-per-ticket goal. The pilot also covered one agent, one stream, two weeks, and says nothing about the other four queues.","how_to_resolve":"If the triage desk is to be considered, identify the offsetting reduction and get finance approval before a pilot, as the objectives require; otherwise record it as out of budget rather than out of evidence."},{"id":"C14","topic":"Whether any intervention has evidence on time-to-resolution, the actual decision metric","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-06ff9877","quote":"No intervention has been tested with time-to-resolution as its primary measure.","locator":"prior_experiments.md, Not attempted"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-8dc73255","quote":"Misroutes fall from 1,382 to 552, a reduction of 60.1%.","locator":"classifier_trial_report.md, Results on the held-out set"},"summary":"The decision question is about time-to-resolution, but the strongest available result is an offline routing-accuracy result. The trial states the link is not measured: \"Any statement about the effect on resolution time is an inference from the accuracy result, not a measurement of it.\" The one experiment that did measure resolution time, the intake form A/B, found 20.8 vs 21.1 hours and no meaningful difference.","how_to_resolve":"Run the shadow period the trial team recommends — classifier and rules engine both logged, rules applied — and measure accuracy and time-to-resolution on the same tickets, allowing for the 26-hour analytics lag before any read."}]}

support_ticket_routing::missing_evidence.text: {"gaps":[{"id":"GAP-001","question":"What effect does improved routing accuracy actually have on median and p90 time-to-resolution?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"The decision outcome is stated in resolution-time terms, but the strongest piece of evidence (the classifier trial) measured only routing accuracy and explicitly could not measure resolution time, because no ticket was ever routed by the classifier and no customer was affected. The 14.2h vs 51.8h correctly-routed/misrouted gap is observational and cannot be adjusted for ticket difficulty, since no complexity or effort score exists on tickets. So the entire causal link from accuracy to the target metric is unmeasured, not small.","how_to_obtain":"Run the shadow period the trial team recommended: classifier and rules engine both decide on live tickets, rules decision applied, both logged; then a controlled ramp where the classifier's decision is applied to a randomised share of tickets, with median and p90 time-to-resolution as the primary measure and reassignments per ticket as secondary. Allow for the 26-hour analytics lag.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-002","question":"What does it cost to run, serve, retrain and monitor the classifier in production, per ticket and per quarter?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"'Hold cost per ticket flat' is a hard constraint and a board-reported measure, and D-2025-11 forbids new ML infrastructure spend in FY26. The trial explicitly did not estimate production or retraining cost and ran on unmetered shared batch capacity. The one confident cost claim on record ('pays for itself inside a quarter') was made with no model behind it. Without a figure nobody can tell whether the classifier satisfies or breaches the binding constraint.","how_to_obtain":"Ask support-engineering and the Modelyard owners for a costed estimate: incremental compute for a third 340 MB CPU model at current arrival volume, retraining cadence and cost, engineering time for quarterly re-evaluation required by the governance policy, plus monitoring. Have finance confirm whether it lands inside or outside D-2025-11.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-003","question":"What would a triage desk cost in agent hours and headcount reallocation, and does finance approve it?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"The manual triage pilot is the only intervention with a demonstrated accuracy figure near 94%, and the corpus derives a rough five-full-time-router requirement from one agent's throughput. But headcount is frozen and any additional agents must be funded by a reduction elsewhere with prior finance approval. No costed proposal, no source of the offsetting reduction, and no finance position exist. The option cannot be ranked against the classifier without them.","how_to_obtain":"Have support-operations produce a staffing and cost model for triage at full intake volume, and obtain a written finance position on whether the offsetting reduction is available before any pilot.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-004","question":"Does a triage desk work in the four queues other than Technical Faults, and does one agent's rate hold at volume?","impact":"would_refine_scope","why_it_matters":"The pilot covered only the Technical Faults intake stream, used a single senior agent who knew he was being measured, and ran two weeks. The corpus states plainly that it says nothing about the other four queues and does not establish volume performance. Technical Faults is only 8,940 of 41,880 Q2 rows, so the majority of ticket volume has no triage evidence at all. Scoping a triage intervention to all queues would rest on nothing.","how_to_obtain":"Extend the pilot across all five intake streams with multiple routers over a longer window, blind to measurement where possible, reporting per-queue accuracy and sustained throughput.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-005","question":"What share of the 16.7% volume increase is reopened-issue clone records rather than new customer issues?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"This question was raised in the stakeholder review and nobody had the figure. Clone records did not exist before 2025-10-14, so the year-over-year comparison from 35,900 to 41,880 crosses a definition change and overstates growth by an unquantified amount. Reopen clones also split one customer wait into two shorter recorded resolution times, meaning the reported median and p90 trends are themselves distorted. If most of the growth and most of the resolution-time deterioration is reopen behaviour, the right intervention may be reopen reduction rather than routing at all.","how_to_obtain":"Recompute distinct-issue volume and resolution time for every period on a like-for-like basis (subtracting reopen_rows_included and stitching reopened_from chains into single customer waits), and restate the 2025-Q2 baseline accordingly.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-006","question":"Why are 14% of tickets reopened within 14 days?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"Reopens are the largest single distortion in the outcome metrics and a plausible driver of true customer wait, yet no reason code and no free-text reason is captured anywhere, and the corpus records that no analysis of why tickets are reopened exists and no reopen-reduction test has been run. A competing intervention aimed at resolution quality cannot even be formulated, let alone compared, until this is characterised.","how_to_obtain":"Manually review a random sample of reopened-issue pairs to categorise causes (premature closure, incomplete fix, misroute, customer follow-up), and add a reason field at closure/reopen in Relay.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-007","question":"Does reassignment degrade customer satisfaction, and does routing automation change resolution quality?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"'Do not degrade resolution quality' is an explicit constraint, and the concern that a model sending a ticket to the wrong place costs customer trust was raised directly in the review. The csat_after_reassignment field exists in routing_metrics.csv but was never populated — blank, not zero. There is no other quality or satisfaction measure in the corpus at all, so the constraint is currently unverifiable in either direction.","how_to_obtain":"Populate csat_after_reassignment from the existing survey pipeline for historical quarters if responses were collected, or instrument collection now; define a resolution-quality proxy (reopen rate, reassignment count, first-contact resolution) to be tracked through any shadow or ramp period.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-008","question":"How does classifier accuracy hold outside the January–March window?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"The held-out set is entirely 2026-Q1, a window shaped by the post-holiday returns peak, and the trial states that whether accuracy holds across the rest of the year is untested. The headline 88.5% therefore describes one seasonal ticket mix. A materially lower figure in other quarters would weaken the case without necessarily overturning it, given the rules engine's demonstrated ceiling.","how_to_obtain":"Re-evaluate the trained model on held-out tickets from other quarters available in the warehouse (text exists from 2023-04 onward), and make seasonal re-evaluation part of the quarterly cycle the governance policy already requires.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-009","question":"What do agents do when shown a routing decision they disagree with, and what is the rate of override?","impact":"would_refine_scope","why_it_matters":"'Do not remove agent control' is a constraint and the governance policy requires single-action override. The trial never showed a prediction to an agent and so could not measure this, and agent actions are logged as state transitions only — there is no record anywhere of disagreement, only of the reassignment itself. Whether displaying model confidence increases or suppresses appropriate overrides is unknown, which affects how the interface should be scoped, not whether to proceed.","how_to_obtain":"During the shadow or ramp period, instrument the routing surface to record whether the model decision was displayed, and add an explicit override signal distinct from ordinary reassignment; interview agents after the first weeks.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-010","question":"What are median and p90 time-to-resolution, reassignments and reopen rate broken down by queue and by both dimensions together?","impact":"would_refine_scope","why_it_matters":"Resolution time exists per queue for only two of five queues in 2026-Q2 (technical_faults 34.1h, billing_and_payments 11.3h), and p90 exists only at the 'all' segment for two periods. Reassignment churn has no queue breakdown at all, and the misrouted/correctly-routed split is not crossed with queue. Since the classifier loses to the rules engine in Billing & Payments and wins largest in Account & Access, the sensible scope is likely a per-queue hybrid — which cannot be designed without per-queue outcome data.","how_to_obtain":"Extend routing_metrics.csv to a full queue-by-metric grid for median, p90, reassignments per ticket and reopen rate, and cross the misrouted/correctly-routed segment with queue.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-011","question":"Is the vendor option viable at all — on what sample and taxonomy was 92% measured, and what does the data protection assessment conclude?","impact":"would_refine_scope","why_it_matters":"AutoTriage is nominally a third option, but the vendor material states no sample, no baseline, no queue taxonomy and no industry, and no independent evaluation was offered. Separately, the vendor would process ticket text on its own infrastructure, which engages both the in-region processing requirement and the mandatory pre-sharing data protection assessment that currently takes six to eight weeks. Without either the evaluation detail or the assessment, the option cannot be compared and cannot even be trialled.","how_to_obtain":"Request from Tessarine a like-for-like evaluation on the five-queue taxonomy with a stated sample and baseline; in parallel ask legal-privacy whether in-region processing is contractually achievable and start the assessment clock only if the answer is yes.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-012","question":"What is the true correct-queue label, as opposed to the resolving queue used as its proxy?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"The trial's labels are the queue the ticket was resolved in, and the report states explicitly that this is a proxy and not the same thing; the audit found 48 of 1,200 tickets where both reviewers judged the resolving queue wrong. Every accuracy figure in the corpus — rules engine and classifier alike — inherits this measurement error, which caps how firmly the 88.5% vs 71.2% comparison can be held even though it affects both arms.","how_to_obtain":"Have support operations adjudicate a larger stratified sample to a gold-standard correct-queue label, and re-score both routers against it to quantify the proxy's bias per queue.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-013","question":"What is the routing accuracy and resolution-time cost of the roughly 9% of Technical Faults tickets carrying a photograph the router cannot see?","impact":"would_refine_scope","why_it_matters":"Attachments are not in the warehouse, so neither the rules engine nor the classifier can act on them, and Technical Faults is both the worst-routed queue (61.8% rules, 82.9% classifier) and the slowest measured queue at 34.1h median. No evidence in the corpus segments performance by attachment presence, so it is unknown whether these tickets are a concentrated pocket of the residual misroutes that no text-based router can fix.","how_to_obtain":"Join attachment presence from the ticket platform onto the held-out trial set and re-score accuracy and resolution time with and without photographs; assess whether making attachments available to the router is a cheaper lever than either candidate.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-014","question":"What concrete rule changes would a fourth expansion pass make, and what accuracy gain do they predict?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"Continued rules tuning is a live option, asserted in the review as reaching 85% with two more passes, but when asked which passes he had in mind the answer was that the team would work it out — no specification exists. Support-engineering's countervailing assessment is that keyword rules have hit their ceiling. Without a named set of candidate rules and an offline estimate of their effect, the option is an opinion rather than a comparable alternative, and dismissing it rests on trend extrapolation alone.","how_to_obtain":"Ask support-engineering to error-analyse the 2026-Q1 misroute set for cases a keyword or pattern rule could resolve, propose specific rules, and replay them offline against the same 4,800-ticket held-out set the classifier was scored on, alongside the growing per-rule review cost.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-015","question":"Does a documented rollback procedure and named accountable owner exist for the classifier, and has the required quarterly re-evaluation cadence been resourced?","impact":"would_refine_scope","why_it_matters":"The governance policy makes these preconditions for production use of any learned model. The trial satisfies the documented offline evaluation on unseen data and data-platform is a plausible owner, but no rollback procedure appears anywhere in the corpus and no owner is formally named for production operation. support_ticket_routing::recommendation::.text: {"recommendation":{"statement":"Prioritise OPT-03: run the trialled classifier in shadow mode on live tickets, with the rules engine still deciding and applying every route, for one full quarter outside the January–March window. Treat it explicitly as a gating measurement, not as an intervention that will move time-to-resolution this half — by construction it changes nothing for customers. Its purpose is to (a) confirm the 88.5% vs 71.2% offline accuracy gap holds on live traffic and a different ticket mix, (b) produce the first metered run/retrain cost figure, which no option currently has, and (c) create the agent-disagreement signal that today does not exist. Alongside it, the team may run OPT-10 (Billing / Account & Access ownership playbook) as a near-zero-cost parallel action, but on the honest footing that no training or process intervention in this corpus has any measured effect — it is a cheap bet, not an evidenced one. Do not fund OPT-08 (classifier as primary router) yet: it is blocked by D-2025-06 as written, its cost is unestimated against a board-reported cost-per-ticket measure, and the accuracy-to-TTR link is inferred rather than measured. OPT-05 and OPT-07 are blocked by headcount freeze and by the mandatory data protection assessment respectively, and neither block is in the team's gift to clear this quarter. support_ticket_routing::challenger::v1.text: {"findings":[{"question":"claims_supported","verdict":"concern","explanation":"Most numeric claims resolve, but three load-bearing ones overreach their sources. (1) C8 asserts shadow mode 'needs no new infrastructure' and fits the 400 ms budget — but the 41 ms/118 ms figures were measured 'on the trial hardware' in an offline batch run, and the documented shadow precedent is rules-v2 vs rules-v3 inside one service, not a Modelyard-hosted model called from the ticket-creation path. Nothing in evidence shows online serving from Modelyard inside the 400 ms handler, or the engineering cost of wiring it. (2) C1 is labelled [fact] but its operative clause — that a fourth expansion pass would achieve no more — is support-engineering's forward-looking assessment, which the claim set itself classifies as stakeholder_opinion (C-010). (3) C15's 'wrong about a third of the time' converts a concordance-with-resolving-queue statistic (64.3%) into a correctness rate, when the same corpus documents that the resolving queue is only a proxy for the correct queue.","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-8dc73255","quote":"Median inference time on the trial hardware was 41 ms per ticket, CPU only, with a 99th percentile of 118 ms."},{"evidence_id":"EV-ac98dec8","quote":"It can be run in shadow alongside a second router: both produce a decision, one is applied, both are logged. Shadow mode has been used before, for the v3 rollout in November 2024."},{"evidence_id":"EV-79d2ae90","quote":"We do not expect a fourth expansion pass to behave differently from the three before it."},{"evidence_id":"EV-06ff9877","quote":"The share of tickets where the customer-selected category matched the resolving queue rose from 57.1% to 64.3%."}]},{"question":"contradictions_considered","verdict":"concern","explanation":"The corpus's headline conflicts (78% vs 71%, cost payback vs no cost model, vendor 92%, misroute confound, reopen-inflated TTR) are engaged. Two directly adverse items are dropped from the supporting claims. First, reassignments per ticket moved only 0.58 to 0.62 while median TTR rose 3.2 hours — evidence that reassignment churn is not what is driving the metric the decision is about; this appears only in a footnote to OPT-01's risk field and never in the case for a routing-accuracy intervention. Second, the 16.7% volume growth that frames the urgency is inflated by reopen clone records (5,140 of 41,880), so distinct issues barely grew; if the deterioration is reopen-driven, the whole routing track is the wrong lever and OPT-06 should not be a conditional afterthought. Also unresolved: the draft's own OPT-09 assessment states the model 'counts as affecting customer outcomes for change-control purposes', which sits against C9's assertion that shadow mode engages no governance requirement.","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-c6a26def","quote":"value: 0.62","locator":"reassignments_per_ticket 2026-Q2"},{"evidence_id":"EV-133fecfa","quote":"value: 22.6","locator":"median_time_to_resolution_hours 2026-Q2"},{"evidence_id":"EV-e8b9716e","quote":"reopen_rows_included: 5140"},{"evidence_id":"EV-3e2d12e8","quote":"A year-over-year comparison that uses `exported_rows` across that date is comparing two different things and will overstate growth."},{"evidence_id":"EV-46e54a4b","quote":"Any learned model that affects customer outcomes requires, before production use: a named accountable owner, a documented offline evaluation on data the model was not trained on, a documented rollback procedure, and re-evaluation at least quarterly thereafter."}]},{"question":"preference_as_evidence","verdict":"concern","explanation":"The draft is admirably explicit about Marek Vandal's 85% claim (C2) and the staff engineer's payback claim (C7). But it repeats the same error in its own favour: C1 presents support-engineering's expectation about a fourth pass as fact, and the selected option is precisely the course of action recommended by the team that built and presented the classifier — a recorded opinion from an interested party, not a finding. That provenance is nowhere disclosed in the support rationale. No individual crew has been flagged for an accuracy intervention.","locator":"Picking accuracy section, 2026-Q2 review"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-73cc4f66","quote":"value: 7.3","locator":"period 2026-Q2, metric shift_mispick_rate, segment night_shift_c"},"summary":"The quarterly review states shift performance is consistent, while the shift-level metric series for the same quarter records night_shift_c at 7.3 per 1,000 lines against day_shift_a at 2.3 (EV-c3502fcb) and twilight_shift_b at 3.7 (EV-563221be).","how_to_resolve":"Confirm which series the review author used: if the review was written from the site-level rate only, the 'consistent across shifts' line is unsupported. Recompute shift rates from 2026-Q2 mispick counts and lines picked per shift and restate."},{"id":"C-02","topic":"Whether the shift gap is a crew/tenure effect or an aisle-mix effect","kind":"scope_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-320c5fb9","quote":"Give me permanent heads instead of agency and this goes away. You cannot run an accurate operation on people who have been here four months.","locator":"Ilse Brandt, Night Shift Manager (Shift C)"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-7b7275e6","quote":"rate_per_1000_lines: 1.5","locator":"period 2026-Q2, shift night_shift_c, aisle_range all_other_aisles"},"summary":"Night shift is blamed on agency labour and short tenure (61% agency, 4 months median tenure per EV-1a4b2e68 and EV-14039eca). But outside aisles 31 to 44 the night crew records 1.5 per 1,000, level with day shift's 1.6 in the same aisle group (EV-eadc3cdb); night shift also picks 71% of its lines in aisles 31 to 44 (EV-f198fa5a). The two statements describe different populations: whole-shift totals versus aisle-matched comparison.","how_to_resolve":"Compare shift rates within aisle group (31-44 versus all other aisles) and, if possible, within confusable-pair faces only. If the gap disappears once aisle mix is held constant, the driver is exposure to those faces, not crew composition."},{"id":"C-03","topic":"Whether mispicks were already rising before the February reslot","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-320c5fb9","quote":"We already looked at that. The numbers were climbing before we moved anything.","locator":"Marcus Adeyemi, on the February reslot"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-6d7fc114","quote":"value: 2.5","locator":"period 2026-01, metric aisle_31_44_mispick_rate"},"summary":"The director states the rate was climbing pre-reslot. The aisle 31-44 monthly series shows 2.6 in Nov 2025 (EV-fe7268b4), 2.7 in Dec, 2.5 in Jan 2026, then 6.4 in Feb (EV-b2b6245b, noted 'reslot executed 2026-02-09') and 9.1 in Mar (EV-466711a2).","how_to_resolve":"Agree which series and which segment the claim refers to. The site-level rate did rise from 2.5 (2025-Q3) to 2.6 to 3.0, so a site-level reading is arguably 'climbing'; the aisle 31-44 series is flat until February. Pin the claim to a named segment and period before it is used."},{"id":"C-04","topic":"Whether volume growth explains the rise in mispicks","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-b35f27bd","quote":"Mispicks are up from 2.6 per 1,000 in 2025-Q4. The increase tracks the volume growth of the past two quarters.","locator":"Picking accuracy section"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-9190b82c","quote":"value: 2400000","locator":"period 2026-Q2, metric lines_picked, segment all"},"summary":"The review attributes the rise to volume growth, but lines picked fell from 2,500,000 in 2025-Q4 (EV-f83a330b) to 2,300,000 in 2026-Q1 (EV-a3bbb525) and 2,400,000 in 2026-Q2. The mispick rate is already volume-normalised.","how_to_resolve":"Ask the review author for the volume figures used. If they are the same lines_picked series, the attribution fails on its own numbers; note instead that the share of lines in aisles 31 to 44 rose from 12.0% to 29.6% (EV-b60c4443, EV-52ad2177), which is a mix change, not a volume change."},{"id":"C-05","topic":"Largest error type — site-wide versus aisles 31 to 44 versus the rest of the site","kind":"scope_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-a7cded47","quote":"error_type: wrong_quantity","locator":"period 2026-Q2, aisle_range all_other_aisles, share_of_group_percent: 40.5"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-c15b62e0","quote":"error_type: wrong_item_similar_sku","locator":"period 2026-Q2, aisle_range aisles_31_44, share_of_group_percent: 64.0"},"summary":"Both 'biggest problem' statements can be true of different segments. In all other aisles wrong_quantity is the largest type at 40.5% of that group; in aisles 31 to 44 wrong_item_similar_sku is largest at 64.0%; site-wide, wrong_item_similar_sku leads at 52.0% (EV-3552e637) against wrong_quantity at 23.0% (EV-2081d019).","how_to_resolve":"State the segment whenever the 'biggest' error type is quoted. For a site-wide intervention decision, weight by absolute counts: 4,335 similar-SKU mispicks in aisles 31-44 versus 1,095 quantity mispicks elsewhere."},{"id":"C-06","topic":"Which error type is the largest — 2025-Q4 versus 2026-Q2","kind":"temporal_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-320c5fb9","quote":"Quantity errors are our biggest problem. Always have been.","locator":"Devon Achebe, Continuous Improvement Lead"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-3552e637","quote":"share_of_group_percent: 52.0","locator":"period 2026-Q2, aisle_range all_aisles, error_type wrong_item_similar_sku"},"summary":"The 'always have been' claim matches the older row: in 2025-Q4 wrong_quantity was the largest site-wide type at 37.0% (EV-9ca16ade) against wrong_item_similar_sku at 25.0% (EV-65af2aee). The claim is stale rather than false — it belongs to 2025-Q4 and earlier.","how_to_resolve":"Date-stamp the claim. Pull the error-type mix for 2026-Q1 as well to see exactly when the crossover occurred relative to the February reslot."},{"id":"C-07","topic":"Current site mispick rate","kind":"temporal_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-8f5d5027","quote":"The current site mispick rate is 2.6 per 1,000 lines.","locator":"Current position, site objectives updated 2026-01-20"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-ef4cc69c","quote":"value: 3.9","locator":"period 2026-Q2, metric site_mispick_rate, segment all"},"summary":"The objectives document quotes 2.6 per 1,000 as current. That figure is the 2025-Q4 row of the metric series (EV-b773a9fd); the series then runs 3.0 in 2026-Q1 and 3.9 in 2026-Q2. The prose is stale, belonging to 2025-Q4, not wrong for its period.","how_to_resolve":"Refresh the objectives document against the 2026-Q2 series, and restate the gap to the FY26 target of 2.0 per 1,000 from the current 3.9 rather than 2.6."},{"id":"C-08","topic":"Whether pick-to-light demonstrably improved accuracy","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-1d7f300b","quote":"aisles 45 to 52 recorded 2.1 mispicks per 1,000 lines in August 2025, against 3.4 per 1,000 in November 2024. In 2026-Q2 the pick-to-light aisles run at 1.7 per 1,000, essentially level with the 1.6 recorded across all other (non pick-to-light) aisles (EV-2573868f), which had no such installation.","how_to_resolve":"Run the comparison the original write-up omitted: pick-to-light aisles versus matched non-PTL ambient aisles over the same months. The log itself records that 'No concurrent control aisles were used and no other comparison period was reported.'"},{"id":"C-09","topic":"Whether the 38% pick-to-light reduction is a like-for-like comparison","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-320c5fb9","quote":"Devon also recirculated the 2025 pick-to-light write-up, said the system paid for itself in eighteen months, and argued for extending it.","locator":"Devon Achebe, Continuous Improvement Lead"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-f398b395","quote":"note: synthetic - November is the annual peak","locator":"period 2024-11, metric monthly_lines_picked, value 1072000"},"summary":"The 38% figure compares August 2025 with November 2024. November is the annual volume peak with 39% agency labour (EV-69832347); August is the annual trough at 688,000 lines with 21% agency labour (EV-4b4efb76, EV-ce697b02). Peak-versus-trough months are not comparable periods, so the reduction may be seasonal rather than caused by pick-to-light.","how_to_resolve":"Recompute the pick-to-light effect month-on-matched-month (August 2025 versus August 2024, or November versus November), and control for agency labour share, before any extension business case relies on the 38% figure."},{"id":"C-10","topic":"Whether the reslot's accuracy effect was measured","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-1d7f300b","quote":"No accuracy impact was expected, and none was measured before or after the move.","locator":"D-2026-01 reslot of aisles 31 to 44"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-2fd0b80a","quote":"note: synthetic - before the February 2026 reslot","locator":"period 2025-Q4, aisle_range aisles_31_44, rate_per_1000_lines 2.7"},"summary":"The decision log says nothing was measured before or after the reslot, but the mispick log carries pre-reslot rows for the same aisle group (2.7 per 1,000 in 2025-Q4) and post-reslot rows for 2026-Q2 (9.5 per 1,000, EV-3ee7004b), plus a continuous monthly series.","how_to_resolve":"Distinguish 'no measurement was designed as part of the decision' from 'no data exists'. Confirm the monthly aisle 31-44 series is on a consistent definition across the February cutover, then use it as the before/after read."},{"id":"C-11","topic":"How much of the workforce finds the new layout confusing","kind":"scope_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-320c5fb9","quote":"The cards say most of our pickers find the new layout confusing.","locator":"Devon Achebe, Continuous Improvement Lead"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-979e7748","quote":"The 22 respondents are not a random sample of the 340 picking associates.","locator":"Associate feedback card, limitations"},"summary":"'Most of our pickers' is asserted of the 340 picking associates. The underlying data is 15 of 22 respondents at a voluntary shift meeting — a majority of that self-selected group, not of the workforce.","how_to_resolve":"Rerun the question as a census or random sample across all three shifts, or restate the finding as '15 of 22 volunteers at one meeting'."},{"id":"C-12","topic":"Whether separating the confusable pairs needs no purchase or approval","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-320c5fb9","quote":"We can move slots ourselves in the workbench. It is a weekend job. Nobody needs to buy anything.","locator":"Ruth Oyelaran, Warehouse Systems Analyst"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-6562cfc0","quote":"Any slot move involving allergen-segregated or temperature-controlled stock requires a documented food-safety review before the move.","locator":"Food safety section"},"summary":"The systems view is that pair separation is a self-service weekend task; governance requires a documented food-safety review, typically two weeks, and the study records that four of the 41 pairs sit in allergen-segregated stock (EV-979e7748). No purchase is needed, but the schedule claim and the review requirement conflict.","how_to_resolve":"Split the work: 34 non-allergen adjacent pairs can proceed on the workbench path; the 4 allergen pairs need the food-safety review booked first. Also cost the effort properly — 11 minutes average per physical face move (EV-b7efb287) against 38 pairs, which Ruth confirmed she had not worked out."},{"id":"C-13","topic":"Whether Shift A is unaffected","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-320c5fb9","quote":"My numbers are fine. Whatever is going on, it is not on my shift.","locator":"Tomas Lindqvist, Day Shift Manager (Shift A)"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-a4beb4a0","quote":"rate_per_1000_lines: 9.5","locator":"period 2026-Q2, shift day_shift_a, aisle_range aisles_31_44"},"summary":"Day shift's whole-shift rate is 2.3 per 1,000 (EV-c3502fcb), the best of the three. But within aisles 31 to 44 day shift records 9.5 per 1,000, indistinguishable from twilight's 9.4 (EV-882e5814) and night's 9.6 (EV-369cf5ac). Day shift looks clean only because 9% of its lines are in that aisle group (EV-2d961c97).","how_to_resolve":"Present shift performance aisle-adjusted alongside the headline rate, so that exposure to aisles 31-44 is separated from crew performance."},{"id":"C-14","topic":"Status of the pack-station accuracy audit","kind":"temporal_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-1d7f300b","quote":"The suspension was described as temporary.","locator":"D-2026-02, decision dated 2026-01-05"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-b35f27bd","quote":"The pack-station accuracy audit was suspended on 2026-01-05 to release two associates for the reslot. It has not restarted.","locator":"Quality assurance section, 2026-07-09"},"summary":"A suspension recorded as temporary in January was still in force at the July review, and the interception metric field for 2026-Q2 was never populated (EV-5e7ea944). Both statements are true of their own dates; the 'temporary' framing no longer describes the situation.","how_to_resolve":"Set a restart date or formally reclassify the suspension as permanent. Until interception counts resume, the mispick log understates total error volume and any before/after measurement of a new intervention has no pack-line comparator."}]}

Ruth Oyelaran was asked directly and had not worked it out.","how_to_obtain":"Warehouse-systems and industrial-engineering to build a bottom-up estimate: faces to move, minutes per move, shift/overtime rate, cube and pallet-height feasibility check in the Corvus workbench, and the net travel-time change from breaking the velocity-based slotting. Sign-off from the regional finance partner as required by the FY26 objectives.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-03","question":"Can the returns consolidation cage be relocated, where to, and at what cost — i.e. is a full reversal of the February reslot even an option?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"Full reversal (returning the 214 faces to the dock-side bulk area, restoring the 34m median separation) is the most complete remedy and is currently ruled out only because the cage occupies the released 1,100 m². This population is entirely unevidenced.","how_to_obtain":"Join mispick records to labour records at aisle-group level in aggregate form only. Without a unit value, none of the options — $1.4m vision, $610k+ pick-to-light extension, slot separation, restarted pack audit — can be ranked on return, and the September capital submission has no benefit side.","how_to_obtain":"Request the store discrepancy claims series and unit claim cost from finance and the store-support function. If the true added time is affordable, a different and much cheaper answer becomes plausible; if not, it breaches the binding cost-per-line constraint.","how_to_obtain":"Run a timed work-measurement study on a proper sample of scan-verify and check-digit picks, convert to cost per line at site labour rates, and pilot enforcement in a defined aisle group with a concurrent control.
